BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r1.claim: Since delayed punishment is respite rather than neglect and will certainly come, the Prophet should endure their accusations of disbelief, sorcery, and madness until judgment; certainty of their punishment consoles him.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r1.anchor: فاصبر على ما يقولون فيك من كلمات الكفر والنسبة إلى السحر والجنون

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r2.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r2.claim: The objections and denials are part of the Prophet's spiritual training toward the station of patience.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r2.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" على ما يقول أهل الاعتراض والإنكار

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r3.claim: Some say this command to endure was abrogated by the sword verse.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r3.anchor: قال بعضهم : هذا منسوخ بآية السيف

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r4.speaker: الكبير
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r4.claim: Al-Kabir says abrogation is unnecessary because the Prophet could fight and still endure their verbal abuse.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r4.anchor: وفي "الكبير" هذا غير لازم لجواز أن يقاتل ويصبر على ما يسمع منهم من الأذى

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r5.speaker: الراغب
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r5.claim: Al-Raghib defines patience as restraining oneself for what reason and law require or from what they forbid; its name varies by setting, such as courage in battle, broadness of chest in calamity, and concealment in silence.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r5.anchor: قال الراغب : الصبر حبس النفس على ما يقتضيه العقل والشرع

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r6.claim: Tasbih with praise means prayer, using a part for the whole; remembrance soothes the heart and makes grief recede.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r6.anchor: أي : صل حامدا لربك على هدايته وتوفيقه

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r7.speaker: الخبر
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r7.claim: A report says remembrance and glorification until sunrise surpass freeing eighty descendants of Ishmael; he is singled out for his nobility and as ancestor of the Arabs.
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r7.anchor: وفي الخبر "إن الذكر والتسبيح إلى طلوع الشمس أفضل من إعتاق ثمانين رقبة

BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p340#3/r8.claim: Before sunrise means the dawn prayer; before sunset means the noon and afternoon prayers, both after the sun passes its zenith.

BURSEVI:v5p341/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p341/r1.claim: The night prayers are Maghrib and Isha; they are especially virtuous because the heart is more collected and the self inclines to rest, making worship harder.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r1.anchor: فصل والمراد المغرب والعشاء وتقديم الوقت فيهما

BURSEVI:v5p341/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p341/r2.claim: أطراف النهار directs voluntary prayers during the parts of daytime.

BURSEVI:v5p341/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r3.speaker: العيون
BURSEVI:v5p341/r3.claim: Al-Uyun reads the phrase in the accusative with the preceding time expressions and identifies the prayers as Maghrib and repeated Fajr for emphasis; some exegetes instead identify Asr.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r3.anchor: وفي "العيون" هو بالنصب عطف على ما قبله من الظروف

BURSEVI:v5p341/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r4.speaker: الجلالين
BURSEVI:v5p341/r4.claim: Al-Jalalayn identifies before sunset as Asr and the daytime edges as Dhuhr in the second half of the day.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r4.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" قبل غروبها صلاة العصر وأطراف النهار صلاة الظهر

BURSEVI:v5p341/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r5.speaker: الطبري
BURSEVI:v5p341/r5.claim: Al-Tabari identifies before sunset as Asr, night as Isha, and the daytime edges as Dhuhr and Maghrib; Dhuhr touches both halves and Maghrib closes the second.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r5.anchor: وقال الطبري قبل غروبها وهي العصر ومن آناء الليل هي العشاء الآخرة

BURSEVI:v5p341/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r6.speaker: أبو القاسم الفزاري
BURSEVI:v5p341/r6.claim: Al-Fazari cites this interpretation and notes related discussion at the ends of Hud and in Qaf.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r6.anchor: وبهذا احتج الشيخ أبو القاسم الفزاري في "الأسئلة المقحمة"

BURSEVI:v5p341/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p341/r7.claim: لعلك ترضى attaches to tasbih: worship at these times in hope that God grants contentment and gladdens the heart.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r7.anchor: أي : سبح في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عنده تعالى ما ترضى به نفسك

BURSEVI:v5p341/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r8.speaker: الكاشفي
BURSEVI:v5p341/r8.claim: Kashifi says the most likely promised honor that satisfies the Prophet is intercession for his community, supported by the promise that his Lord will give until he is content.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r8.anchor: وقال الكاشفي : (خوشنودى در اصح اقوال بكرامتى ماشدكه خداى تعالى اورا عطا دهد

BURSEVI:v5p341/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p341/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p341/r9.claim: Tasbih is seeking support against deniers; prayer is the strongest remedy for pain, the Prophet turned to it when distressed, and this verse gathers the five prayers.
BURSEVI:v5p341/r9.anchor: واعلم أن الاشتغال بالتسبيح استنصار من المسبح للنصر على المكذبين وأن الصلاة أعظم ترياق

BURSEVI:v5p342/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r1.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p342/r1.claim: Jarir reports the Prophet compared the believers' vision of God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r1.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فرأى القمر ليلة البدر

BURSEVI:v5p342/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r2.claim: The reading with a doubled mīm derives from mutual crowding: people will not crowd or press one another to see; a tāʾ is omitted from the original form.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r2.anchor: بتشديد الميم من الضم أي : لا يضم بعضكم بعضا ولا يقول أرنيه

BURSEVI:v5p342/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r3.claim: An alternate light-mīm reading derives from injustice: no one will be excluded from the vision, and all share equally in it.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r3.anchor: وروى بتخفيف الميم من الضيم وهو الظلم فالتاء مضمومة

BURSEVI:v5p342/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r4.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p342/r4.claim: A hadith says Isha and Fajr are the heaviest prayers for hypocrites, who would attend even crawling if they knew their reward.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن أثقل الصلاة على المنافقين صلاة العشاء والفجر

BURSEVI:v5p342/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r5.claim: A report promises broad spiritual and worldly benefits for keeping the five prayers in congregation and severe losses for treating them lightly.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r5.anchor: يقال : من داوم على الصلوات الخمس في الجماعة

BURSEVI:v5p342/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r6.speaker: النبي عليه السلام
BURSEVI:v5p342/r6.claim: A hadith calls the Muslim community one shown mercy and says God averts calamities through their sincerity, prayers, supplication, and weak members.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r6.anchor: وفي الحديث : "أمتي أمة مرحومة" وإنما يدفع الله عنهم البلايا بإخلاصهم

BURSEVI:v5p342/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r7.speaker: قتادة
BURSEVI:v5p342/r7.claim: Qatada reports that Daniel said a people praying the prayer of Muhammad's community would have spared Noah's people from drowning, Ad from the wind, and Thamud from the blast.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r7.anchor: وعن قتادة أن دانيال النبي عليه السلام نعت أمة محمد فقال

BURSEVI:v5p342/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p342/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p342/r8.claim: A believer should remain constant in prayer, supplication, and seeking refuge with God.
BURSEVI:v5p342/r8.anchor: فعلى المؤمن أن لا ينفك عن الصلاة والدعاء والالتجاء إلى الله تعالى

QASHANI:20:129-130/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:129-130/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:129-130/r1.claim: A prior decree prevents this community’s destruction in worldly life because its Prophet is a prophet of mercy; otherwise annihilation would follow, as the cited verse says.
QASHANI:20:129-130/r1.anchor: قضاء سابق أن لا يستأصل هذه الأمة بالدمار والعذاب في الدنيا لكون نبيهم نبي الرحمة

QASHANI:20:129-130/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:129-130/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:129-130/r2.claim: The Prophet should be patient through God, since his opponents are governed by what God decreed and remain captive to divine power.
QASHANI:20:129-130/r2.anchor: فإنك تراهم جارين على ما قضى الله عليهم، مأسورين في أسر قهره

QASHANI:20:129-130/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:129-130/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:129-130/r3.claim: Glorification strips the self of its own qualities while it bears the Lord’s qualities; this manifestation is true praise.
QASHANI:20:129-130/r3.anchor: نزه ذاتك بتجريدها عن صفاتها متلبسا بصفات ربك، فإن ظهورها عليك هو الحمد الحقيقي

QASHANI:20:129-130/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:129-130/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:129-130/r4.claim: Before sunrise and sunset mark the spirit’s disclosure and concealment in the heart’s station; glorifying there erases the heart’s qualities.
QASHANI:20:129-130/r4.anchor: في مقام القلب حال تجلي الصفات، فإن تسبيح الله هناك محو صفات القلب

QASHANI:20:129-130/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:129-130/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:129-130/r5.claim: Night spells are the ego’s dark, veiling shifts, while day’s edges are the spirit illuminating the heart; purification and refinement lead toward contentment.
QASHANI:20:129-130/r5.anchor: أي: أوقات غلبات صفات النفس المظلمة والتلوينات الحاجبة

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r1.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والكسائي
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r1.claim: Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read turḍā with a ḍamma on tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r1.anchor: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والكسائي: (لعلك ترضى)

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r2.speaker: الباقون
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r2.claim: The remaining readers, including the familiar transmission from Ḥafṣ, read tarḍā with fatḥa on tāʾ.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الباقون، وهبيرة عن حفص عن عاصم

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r3.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r3.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r3.claim: The fatḥa reading is supported by the promise that the Prophet will be pleased; the ḍamma reading evokes the description of a prophet as pleasing to God and can mean being pleased with obedience or God's gift of a high rank.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p252#2/r3.anchor: حجة من فتح التاء قوله: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

QIRAAT-ER:20:130:27#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:20:130:27#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:20:130:27#1/r1.claim: The passive makes satisfaction something granted or approved by God rather than self-achieved.
QIRAAT-ER:20:130:27#1/r1.anchor: shifts agency from addressee to God; satisfaction becomes something granted, not self-achieved

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r1.claim: Qatada maps the times to prayer: before sunrise is Fajr, before sunset Asr, night intervals Maghrib and Isha, and day edges Dhuhr.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس ﴾ قال هي صلاة الفجر ﴿ وقبل غروبها ﴾ صلاة العصر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the periods before sunrise and sunset refer to the obligatory prayers.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p21#4/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى ﴿ قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها ﴾ قال الصلاة المكتوبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r7.claim: God tells Muhammad to bear Quraysh’s abusive speech and to glorify and praise God, either in words or through declaring Him free of their false claims.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r7.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بالصبر على ما يقول مشركو قريش، وهم الذين عاد الضمير عليهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r8.claim: Abu Muslim reads the command as glorifying and exalting God, rather than prescribing specific wording.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r8.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم: لا يبعد حمله على التنزيه والإجلال

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r9.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r9.claim: Al-Razi prefers the glorification reading because it follows the command to endure denials and counteracts their claims of disbelief and association.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r9.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله الرازي: وهذا القول أقرب إلى الظاهر وإلى ما تقدم ذكره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r10.speaker: قول في التفسير
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r10.claim: A prayer interpretation maps the times to dawn, afternoon, evening, nightfall, and midday prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r10.anchor: فقبل طلوع الشمس صلاة الصبح وقبل غروبها صلاة العصر ومن آناء الليل المغرب والعتمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r11.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r11.claim: Ibn Atiyya allows the wording to mean saying subhan Allah and praise after dawn prayer through the forenoon prayer and before sunset.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p397/r11.anchor: قال ابن عطية: ويحتمل اللفظ أن يراد قول سبحان الله وبحمده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r1.speaker: رسول الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says that whoever glorifies God seventy times at sunset has his sins erased.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r1.anchor: فقد قال عليه السلام: «من سبح عند غروب الشمس سبعين تسبيحة غربت بذنوبه»

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari maps before sunset to noon and afternoon, night portions to nightfall prayer, and day edges to sunset and dawn prayers.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وقبل غروبها يعني الظهر والعصر لأنهما واقعتان في النصف الأخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says night worship is especially meritorious because it allows focus and privacy, and is harder than using the body’s resting time; he links it with other night-worship verses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r3.anchor: وذلك أن أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل لاجتماع القلب وهدو الرجل والخلو بالرب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r4.claim: One explanation compares the plural edges of day to poetic dual forms, despite day having only two edges.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r5.speaker: قول ثان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r5.claim: Another takes the plural literally: dawn is one edge, noon and afternoon another, and sunset and nightfall a third.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r5.anchor: وقيل: هو على حقيقة الجمع الفجر الطرف الأول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r6.speaker: قول ثالث
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r6.claim: Another account counts four edges at sunrise, sunset, solar noon, and the sun’s pause at noon.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r6.anchor: وقيل: النهار له أربعة أطراف عند طلوع الشمس، وعند غروبها، وعند زوال الشمس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r7.speaker: قول رابع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r7.claim: Another says midday prayer straddles the two day edges while sunset marks a third edge.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r7.anchor: وقيل: الظهر في آخر طرف النهار الأول، وأول طرف النهار الآخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r8.speaker: قول خامس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r8.claim: Other readings explain the plural by treating day as a recurring genus or by using edges to mean hours.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r8.anchor: وقيل: يجعل النهار للجنس فلكل يوم طرف فيتكرر بتكرره. وقيل: المراد بالأطراف الساعات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r9.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r9.claim: The majority read the word for edges in the accusative, coordinating it with night portions; Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read it in the genitive, coordinating it with night portions grammatically.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: وأطراف بنصب الفاء وهو معطوف على ومن آناء الليل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r10.claim: The hope of being pleased means receiving a reward that one will see, expressed as hope rather than certainty; another view makes divine hope necessarily fulfilled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r10.anchor: لعلك ترضى أي تثاب على هذه الأعمال بالثواب الذي تراه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r11.speaker: أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r11.claim: These readers use a passive form meaning that the Lord will make Muhammad pleased.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p398/r11.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان وعصمة

FARRA:v2p195/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p195/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p195/r2.claim: Commentators identify the ends of the day with dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers; the author prefers taking noon and afternoon as one end and dawn as the other, supported by طرفي النهار.
FARRA:v2p195/r2.anchor: وهو أحب الوجهين إلي، لأنه قال (وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل)

FARRA:v2p195/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p195/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p195/r3.claim: وأطراف may be coordinated in the accusative with before sunrise and sunset, or genitive under ومن أطراف النهار; the latter is not reported in recitation.
FARRA:v2p195/r3.anchor: وإن شئت خفضت أطراف تريد وسبحه من الليل ومن أطراف النهار

FARRA:v2p195/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p195/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p195/r4.claim: Hamza read وإدبار السجود; the alif may take fatḥa or kasra, though kasra is best in recitation.
FARRA:v2p195/r4.anchor: وقرأ حمزة وإدبار السجود. ويجوز في الألف الفتح والكسر

FARRA:v2p196/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p196/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p196/r1.claim: ترضى and ترضى mean the same because when one is satisfied one has satisfied another; Hamza and Abdullah's readers use the unprefixed form, while Abu Abd al-Rahman from Asim read with ḍamma on ت.
FARRA:v2p196/r1.anchor: ومعناهما واحد لأنك إذا رضيت فقد أرضيت

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r1.claim: Patience over their words is possible because delayed punishment is respite rather than neglect and will inevitably arrive; it means composure, not abandoning combat.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r1.anchor: من أن تاخير عذابهم ليس باهمال بل امهال وانه لازم لهم البتة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r2.claim: Reading patience as a command to cease fighting would make the verse abrogated, but that is not intended.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r2.anchor: والمراد به عدم الأضطراب لاترك القتال حتى تكون الآية منسوخة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r3.claim: To glorify God with praise means to pray while praising the Lord who brings the Prophet to perfection through guidance and enabling grace.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r3.anchor: أي صل وانت حامد لربك عز وجل الذي يبلغك إلى كمالك على هدايته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r4.claim: “Before sunrise” means the dawn prayer and “before sunset” the sunset prayer; the time phrase most naturally modifies the command to glorify.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r4.anchor: أي صلاة الفجر ( وقبل غروبها ( أي صلاة المغرب

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r5.speaker: جرير
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r5.claim: A Prophetic report from Jarir interprets glorification at these two times as the two prayers.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r5.anchor: وقد أخرج تفسير التسبيح في هذين الوقتين بما ذكر الطبراني

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r6.speaker: فضالة بن وهب الليثي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r6.claim: The Prophet told Fadala to keep the “two ʿasrs,” explaining them as a prayer before sunrise and another before sunset.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r6.anchor: عن فضالة بن وهب الليثي أن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام قال له : حافظ على العصرين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r7.claim: An alternative interprets the pre-sunset period as noon and afternoon prayers; both occur after noon and before sunset, although ordinary usage favors afternoon.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r7.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالتسبيح قبل غروبها صلاتا الظهر والعصر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r8.claim: آناء means the hours or portions of the night; several spellings and forms are reported, with three more common than the form used here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r8.anchor: أي من ساعاته جمع إنى وانو بالياء والواو وكسر الهمزة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r9.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r9.claim: Raghib relates أناه to time in the verse about guests waiting for food, and cites poetry about delaying supper until a star rose.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r9.anchor: قال الله تعالى ( غير ناظرين اناه ) أي وقته

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r10.speaker: الحطيئة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r10.claim: Al-Hutayʾa’s verse uses آنيت for delaying supper and الإناء for the delay.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r10.anchor: وآنيت العشاء إلى سهيل أو الشعرى فطال بي الاناء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r11.claim: One parsing makes “some night hours” a time phrase governed by an implied “rise,” with فسبح coordinated after it; the author finds this strained.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r12.claim: Other parses make it govern فسبح directly, place it in coordination with وإياي فارهبون, or treat فاء as explanatory or additional for necessary sequence.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r12.anchor: وقيل : منصوب بسبح على نسق ( وإياي فارهبون )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p280#3/r13.claim: One reading makes the night-hours phrase the object of فسبح and treats فاء as an added marker that the command necessarily follows.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r1.claim: أطراف النهار may attach to the position of من آناء الليل, or to the earlier phrase قبل طلوع.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r2.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r2.claim: Qatada, as transmitted by Ibn Jarir and others, interprets the daylight prayer as noon; al-Jubbaʾi prefers that view.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r2.anchor: والمراد من التسبيح اطراف النهار على ما أخرج ابن جرير وابن المنذر وغيرهما عن قتادة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r3.claim: The noon prayer is called an edge because it ends the first half of the day and begins the second, or because every day has two such edges.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r3.anchor: ووجه إطلاق الطرف على وقتها بأنه نهاية النصف الأول من النهار وبداية النصف الأخير

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r4.claim: This explanation is strained: the boundary is outside one half but inside the other, the plural implies at least two, and neither half’s edge is the edge of the whole day.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r4.anchor: أن البداية والنهاية فيه ليست على وتيرة واحدة لأن كون ذلك نهاية باعتبار أن النصف الأول انتهى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r5.claim: Another interpretation repeats dawn and sunset prayers, taking the day as sunrise to sunset and its two ends as the points beside its beginning and end.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r5.anchor: وقيل : هذا تكرير لصلاتي الصبح والمغرب ايذانا باختصاصهما بمزيد مزية

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r6.claim: The plural can denote two edges without ambiguity because the day has only two; matching the plural of night hours favors this reading.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r7.speaker: العجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r7.claim: Al-ʿAjjaj’s line uses a dual pair of deserts and their two backs as a poetic parallel for plural wording about two things.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r7.anchor: قول العجاج : ومهمهين فدفدين مرتين ظهراهما مثل ظهور الترسين

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r8.claim: A further option repeats dawn and afternoon prayers, with the daytime beginning at dawn; if it begins at sunrise, the two ends are not parallel.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r8.anchor: وجوز أن يكون تكريرا لصلاتي الصبح والعصر ويراد بالنهار ما بين طلوع الفجر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r9.claim: Some take the phrase as an order for voluntary prayer in the day’s final hours; this shifts away from the apparent meaning and that period’s suitability for prayer is debatable.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r9.anchor: وقيل : هو أمر بالتطوع في الساعات الأخيرة للنهار وفيه صرف الأمر عن ظاهره

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r10.speaker: الخفاجي
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r10.claim: Al-Khafaji says the phrase is governed by the preceding verb without calling فاء additional, since it does not prevent a verb from governing earlier material.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r10.anchor: وذكر الخفاجي أنه معمول لما ذكر من غير حاجة لدعوى زيادة الفاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r11.claim: Night prayer here means the sunset and nightfall prayers; their special importance warrants a renewed command and foregrounding their hours.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p281/r11.anchor: والمراد من التسبيح في بعض آناء الليل صلاة المغرب وصلاة العشاء

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says tasbīḥ with praise may mean uttering the formula ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God,’ or declaring God free of evil and extolling Him in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r1.anchor: الظاهر أن قوله تعالى : ( وسبح بحمد ربك ) أمر بالتسبيح مقرونا بالحمد

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r2.claim: The literal reading is the formula ‘Glory be to God and praise be to God’; the semantic reading declares God transcendent and extols Him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r2.anchor: إما أن يراد اللفظ أي قل سبحان الله والحمد لله أو يراد المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r3.speaker: ابن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r3.claim: A report cited by Ibn ʿAṭiyya says whoever glorifies God seventy times at sunset has his sins depart with the setting sun.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r3.anchor: وفي خبر ذكره ابن عطية من سبح عند غروب الشمس سبعين تسبيحة غربت بذنوبه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r4.speaker: أبو مسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r4.claim: Abū Muslim allows tasbīḥ to mean declaring God transcendent and majestic, occupying oneself with this at the named times.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r4.anchor: وقال أبو مسلم : لا يبعد حمل ذلك على التنزيه والاجلال والمعنى اشتغل بتنزيه الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r5.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r5.claim: Al-ʿIzz ibn ʿAbd al-Salām likewise reads tasbīḥ as transcendence and takes the bāʾ in ‘with praise’ instrumentally.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r5.anchor: وعلى ذلك حمله أيضا العز بن عبد السلام وجعل الباء في قوله سبحانه : ( بحمد ربك )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r6.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r6.claim: For al-ʿIzz, negating deficiencies affirms their opposites, attributes of perfection; praise may be annexed to its agent, object, or by specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r6.anchor: أن ذلك لتعيين سلب صفات النقص لأن من سلب شيئا فقد اثبت ضده واضداد صفات النقص صفات الكمال

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī favors annexing the verbal noun praise to its agent, since complete true praise is God’s praise of Himself.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r7.anchor: ثم استحسن الأول لأن الحمد الحق الكامل حمد الله تعالى نفسه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r8.claim: The apparent parsing takes the bāʾ as accompaniment and praise as a verbal noun whose object is God.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r8.anchor: والمتبادر جعل الباء للملابسة والإضافة من إضافة المصدر إلى المفعول

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r9.speaker: الإمام
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r9.claim: The Imam prefers tasbīḥ as declaring God free of shirk, closest to context because the Prophet is told to endure denial and association of partners.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r9.anchor: واختار الإمام حمل التسبيح على التنزيه من الشرك وقال : أنه اقرب إلى الظاهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r10.claim: An objection says this reading does not explain the specified times; an answer treats them as signs of continual glorification, as at dawn and evening.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r10.anchor: واعترض بأنه لا وجه حينئذ لتخصيص هذه الأوقات بالذكر وايجيب بأن المراد بذكرها الدلالة على الدوام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r11.claim: The author responds that ‘some of the night’ resists a merely continuous reading; the first command may be general and the second particularized for emphasis.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r11.anchor: ورد بأنه يأباه من التبعيضية في قوله سبحانه ( من إناء الليل ) على أن هذه الدلالة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r12.claim: Another view takes tasbīḥ in its apparent sense and praise as prayer, with the time phrase attached to prayer to explain its specification.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r12.anchor: وقيل : يجوز أن يكون المراد بالتسبيح ما هو الظاهر منه ويكون المراد من الحمد الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r13.claim: Prayer fits the command to endure and recalls seeking help through patience and prayer; reports support prayer here.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r13.anchor: بأن الأنسب بالأمر بالصبر الأمر بالصلاة ليكون ذلك ارشادا لما تضمنه قوله تعالى : ( واستعينوا بالصبر والصلاة )

ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r14.claim: Ṭaraf can mean a portion or group of something, as recorded in al-Ṣiḥāḥ and al-Qāmūs.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p282/r14.anchor: يجوز أن يراد بالطرف طائفة من الشئ فانه أحد معانيه كما في الصحاح والقاموس

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r1.claim: If ‘so that you may be pleased’ modifies glorification, it promises a pleasing reward and is evidence God is under no obligation to reward anyone.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r1.anchor: قيل : هو متعلق بسبح أي سبح في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عنده تعالى ماترضى به نفسك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r2.claim: Alternatively, it may modify patience and prayer, with satisfaction meaning worldly victory and the mission’s spread.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r2.anchor: وجوز أن يكون متعلقا بالأمر بالصبر والأمر بالصلاة والمراد ( لعلك ترضى ) في الدنيا بحصول الظفر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r3.speaker: أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وأبو بكر وأبان وعصمة وأبو عمارة عن حفص وأبو زيد عن المفضل وأبو عبيد ومحمد بن عيسى الأصفهاني
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r3.claim: These reciters read tarḍā in the passive, meaning ‘your Lord will make you pleased.’
ALUSI-FULL:v16p283/r3.anchor: وقرا أبو حيوة وطلحة والكسائي وابو بكر وابان وعصمة وابو عمارة عن حفص

MAJAZ:v2p32/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p32/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p32/r4.claim: Ānāʾ al-layl means the hours of night; its singular is ināʾ and plural aḥsāʾ, patterned on ḥisāʾ.
MAJAZ:v2p32/r4.anchor: «ومن آناء الليل» (130) أي ساعات الليل واحدها إنى تقديره حسى والجميع أحساء

MAJAZ:v2p32/r5.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p32/r5.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p32/r5.claim: The Hudhalī poet al-Mutanakhkhal, also called Abū Athīlah, uses inā for an hour of night.
MAJAZ:v2p32/r5.anchor:
وقال المتنخل الهذلى وهو أبو أثيلة:
حلو ومر كعطف القدح مرته ... فى كل إنى قضاه الليل ينتعل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r4.claim: The command to be patient with what people say was abrogated by the fighting verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r4.anchor: {فاصبر على ما يقولون} نسختها آية القتال

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r5.claim: One interpretation of glorifying God is prayer: dawn before sunrise, afternoon before sunset, Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ at night, and Ẓuhr at the edges of the day; Ẓuhr borders both halves around noon.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r5.anchor: {وسبح بحمد ربك} ، أي صل بأمر ربك. وقيل: صل لله بالحمد له والثناء عليه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r6.claim: He interprets the night prayers as occurring at the beginning of night.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أول الليل

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r7.claim: Another schedule takes the night prayer as ʿIshāʾ and the day-edge prayers as Ẓuhr and Maghrib; Ẓuhr lies at both edges of the halves.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p302/r7.anchor: وقيل: المراد من آناء الليل صلاة العشاء، ومن أطراف النهار صلاة الظهر والمغرب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r1.claim: Laki tarḍā can mean the Prophet will be pleased with his reward in the Hereafter; a passive reading means he will be given that reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r1.anchor: قرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم "ترضى" بضم التاء أي تعطى ثوابه.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r2.claim: Other interpretations are that God will be pleased with the Prophet, as in Mary's account, or that the Prophet will be pleased through intercession.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r2.anchor: وقيل: {ترضى} أي يرضاك الله تعالى، كما قال: "وكان عند ربه مرضيا"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r3.claim: The interpretation of being pleased through intercession is linked to the promise that the Prophet will be given until he is pleased.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r3.anchor: وقيل: معنى الآية لعلك ترضى بالشفاعة، كما قال: "ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r4.claim: Jarīr reports the Prophet said believers will see their Lord as plainly as the full moon and urged preserving prayers before sunrise and sunset, then recited this verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p303/r4.anchor: عن قيس بن أبي حازم، عن جرير بن عبد الله قال: كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنظر إلى القمر ليلة البدر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r3.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their words and glorify God with praise, thanking Him for guidance and acknowledging Him as the source of all blessings.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r3.anchor: وصل وأنت حامد لربك على هدايته وتوفيقه

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r4.claim: The prayer schedule includes dawn before sunrise; noon and afternoon, or afternoon alone, before sunset; evening and night during the night's hours, whose calm makes worship especially demanding.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r4.anchor: يعني الظهر والعصر لأنهما في آخر النهار أو العصر وحده

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r5.claim: The night phrase may mean the sunset and night prayers; the night is especially virtuous because the heart is more collected and rest is more inviting, as in 73:6.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r5.anchor: وإنما قدم زمان الليل لاختصاصه بمزيد الفضل فإن القلب فيه أجمع

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r6.claim: The day's ends may repeat dawn and sunset for emphasis, mean noon as the midpoint's endpoint, or refer to voluntary worship throughout daylight; plural wording has several grammatical explanations.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r6.anchor: تكرير لصلاتي الصبح والمغرب إرادة الاختصاص

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r7.speaker: الكسائي وأبو بكر
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r7.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read the last verb in the passive, yielding the sense that your Lord will make you content.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:129-130/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر بالبناء للمفعول أي يرضيك ربك

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r1.claim: The Prophet is to endure mockery and other hostile speech; prayer and remembrance lift the soul toward spiritual excellence and help sustain patience.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r1.anchor: لك من الاستهزاء وغيره . ولما كان الصبر شديدا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r2.claim: Tasbīḥ with praise means worshipping God alone through prayer and remembrance, declaring him free of imperfection while affirming every perfection.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r2.anchor: حامدا له بإثبات كل كمال , وذلك بأن تصلي له خاصة

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r3.claim: Before sunrise means dawn prayer; before sunset can mean both afternoon and noon prayers, while night hours indicate sunset and night prayers.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r3.anchor: أي بصلاة المغرب والعشاء , إيذانا بعظمة صلاة الليل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r4.claim: Night worship is especially excellent because hearts are settled and people are quiet and alone with God, though its greater difficulty makes it more meritorious.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r4.anchor: لأن العبادة إذ ذاك أشق وأدخل في التكليف فكانت افضل عند الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r5.claim: Repeating the command for dawn and afternoon prayers highlights their special merit; the wording also encompasses voluntary prayers throughout day and night.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r5.anchor: وكرر الأمر بصلاتي الصبح والعصر إعلاما بمزيد فضلهما

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r6.claim: Jarir ibn ʿAbd Allah reports that the Prophet compared seeing God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding the prayers before sunrise and sunset; he then recited this verse. The author says it is in both Ṣaḥīḥs.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r6.anchor: ما في الصحيحين عن جرير ابن عبد الله البجلي رضي الله عنه قال : كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r7.claim: The author prefers reading the prayer times as dawn and afternoon before sunrise and sunset, sunset and night during some night hours, and dawn, noon, and afternoon across the day's four endpoints.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r7.anchor: أن يكون المراد بما قبل الطلوع الصبح , وما قبل الغروب العصر فقط

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r8.claim: On this preferred reading, the first and last endpoints are dawn and afternoon prayers and the middle endpoints preparation for prayer and prayer itself; the prepositions mark night portions but are omitted for the active daytime.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r8.anchor: أما الأول والآخر فبالصبح والعصر , وأما الآخران فبالتهيؤ للصلاة ثم الصلاة نفسها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r9.claim: The wording laʿalla keeps the worshipper hopeful rather than secure: God may please the Prophet with the triumph of his religion and fulfillment of all he hopes for in both lives.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p57/r9.anchor: افعل هذا لتكون على رجاء من أن يرضاك ربك فيرضيك في الدنيا والآخرة

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r9.claim: The commanded glorification before sunrise and sunset refers to the prescribed prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r9.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها} قال: هي الصلاة المكتوبة

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r10.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r10.claim: Qatada maps the times to dawn, afternoon, sunset and night, and midday prayers, respectively.
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r10.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس} قال: هي صلاة الفجر {وقبل غروبها} قال: صلاة العصر

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r11.speaker: جرير
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r11.claim: The Prophet identifies the prayers before sunrise and sunset as morning and afternoon prayers.
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r11.anchor: عن جرير عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها} قال: {قبل طلوع الشمس} صلاة الصبح

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r12.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r12.claim: Al-Suddi says this command came before the five prayers were made obligatory.
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r12.anchor: عن السدي في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها} قال: كان هذا قبل أن تفرض الصلاة

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r1.speaker: جرير
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r1.claim: The Prophet says believers will see their Lord as clearly as the moon and urges them to preserve the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r1.anchor: عن جرير قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنكم سترون ربكم كما ترون هذا القمر لا تضامون في رؤيته

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r2.speaker: عمارة بن رومية
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r2.claim: The Prophet says no one who prays before sunrise and before sunset will enter the Fire.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r2.anchor: عن عمارة بن رومية: سمعت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول: لن يلج النار أحد صلى قبل طلوع الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r3.speaker: فضالة بن وهب الليثي
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r3.claim: The Prophet commands him to guard the two ‘asr prayers, meaning the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r3.anchor: عن فضالة بن وهب الليثي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال له: حافظ على العصرين

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r4.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r4.claim: The night glorification and ends of the day are after dawn and at sunset.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r4.anchor: عن عكرمة في قوله: {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار} قال: بعد الصبح وعند غروب الشمس

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r5.claim: The hoped-for satisfaction refers to the reward God will add for the Prophet.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد في قوله: {لعلك ترضى} قال: الثواب فيما يزيدك الله على ذلك

DURR-FULL:v5p611/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r6.claim: Abu ʿAbd al-Rahman recited لعلك ترضى with the tāʾ vowel raised.
DURR-FULL:v5p611/r6.anchor: عن أبي عبد الرحمن أنه قرأ {لعلك ترضى} برفع التاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r1.claim: The sūra is named Ṭā Hā after its two opening letters, written in their muṣḥaf shapes rather than their spoken letter names, as in al-Aʿrāf.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r1.anchor: سميت سورة ( طاها ) باسم الحرفين المنطوق بهما في أولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r2.claim: The name also appears in the Sunna account of ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb’s conversion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r2.anchor: وكذلك وردت تسميتها في كتب السنة في حديث إسلام عمر بن الخطاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r3.speaker: أبو هريرة
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r3.claim: A report in al-Dārimī says God recited Ṭā Hā two thousand years before creating heaven and earth; angels rejoiced for the community to whom it would descend.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r3.anchor: وفي تفسير القرطبي } عن ( مسند الدرامي ) عن أبي هريرة قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r4.speaker: ابن فورك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r4.claim: Ibn Fūrak interprets the report as God making His speech audible to whichever angels He wished to hear it.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r4.anchor: قال ابن فورك : معناه أن الله أظهر كلامه وأسمعه من أراد أن يسمعه من الملائكة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r5.speaker: السخاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r5.claim: Al-Sakhāwī says the sūra is also called Sūrat al-Kalīm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r5.anchor: وذكر في ( الإتقان ) عن السخاوي أنها تسمى أيضا ( سورة الكليم )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r6.speaker: الهذلي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r6.claim: Al-Hudhali’s Complete names it Sūrat Mūsā.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r6.anchor: وفيه عن الهذلي في ( كامله ) أنها تسمى ( سورة موسى )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r7.claim: The majority hold that the whole sūra is Meccan; Ibn ʿAṭiyya and many commentators state this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r7.anchor: وهي مكية كلها على قول الجمهور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.speaker: السخاوي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.claim: Al-Itqān reports an exception for 20:130 and considers 20:131 another likely exception from the Meccan classification.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p179/r8.anchor: وفي ( الإتقان ) أنه استثني منها آية : { فاصبر على ما يقولون وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r3.claim: A fixed term is coordinated with the prior divine word: without both, annihilation would have been inevitable; the term may be worldly punishment such as Badr or punishment after death.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r3.anchor: { وأجل مسمى } عطف على { كلمة } والتقدير : ولولا كلمة وأجل مسمى يقع عنده الهلاك

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r6.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their denials and delayed threat, without hurrying the punishment; their words cover all such rejection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r6.anchor: وفرع على ذلك أمر رسول الله بالصبر على ما يقولون من التكذيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r7.claim: He should devote himself to purifying himself and his household through prayer, disregard the disbelievers’ worldly comforts, and trust that the God-fearing prevail.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r7.anchor: وأمره بأن يقبل على مزاولة تزكية نفسه وتزكية أهله بالصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r8.claim: Tasbīḥ here means prayer because prayer includes glorifying and declaring God free of imperfection.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r8.anchor: فالتسبيح هنا مستعمل في الصلاة لاشتمالها على تسبيح الله وتنزيهه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r9.claim: The bāʾ in bi-ḥamdi rabbika marks accompaniment by the agent; the phrase functions circumstantially as praising the Lord while glorifying Him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p336/r9.anchor: والباء في قوله { بحمد ربك } للملابسة ، وهي ملابسة الفاعل لفعله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r1.claim: The specified times are the prayers: dawn before sunrise; noon and afternoon before sunset, or afternoon alone; and from nightfall, sunset and night prayers, as clarified by mass-transmitted Sunna.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r1.anchor: والأوقات المذكورة هي أوقات الصلوات ، وهي وقت الصبح قبل طلوع الشمس

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r2.claim: Some take the two times before sunset as only the afternoon prayer, with noon included under the ends of the day.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r2.anchor: وقيل المراد صلاة العصر . وأما الظهر فهي قوله : { وأطراف النهار } كما سيأتي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r3.claim: Min in min ānāʾ al-layl marks the starting point and attaches to fasabbiḥ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r3.anchor: و { من } في قوله { من آناء الليل } ابتدائية متعلقة بفعل ( فسبح )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r4.claim: The fronted time phrase receives emphasis, so fa is used as if the verb were a conditional response, as in the Prophetic command about both parents and in 17:79.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r4.anchor: وأدخلت الفاء على { فسبح } لأنه لما قدم عليه الجار والمجرور للاهتمام شابه تقديم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r5.claim: Night hours receive special emphasis because people tend toward rest then and may neglect prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r5.anchor: ووجه الاهتمام بآناء الليل أن الليل وقت تميل فيه النفوس إلى الدعة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r6.claim: Ānāʾ al-layl means its hours; Ibn ʿĀshūr lists singular forms in ini, inu, inā, and anāʾ, with plural ānāʾ on the afʿāl pattern.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r6.anchor: وآناء الليل : ساعاته . وهو جمع إني بكسر الهمزة وسكون النون وياء في آخره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r7.claim: Wa-aṭrāfa al-nahār is accusative, coordinated with before sunrise; ṭaraf is an endpoint.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r7.anchor: وقوله وأطراف النهار } بالنصب عطف على قوله { قبل طلوع الشمس }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r8.claim: One interpretation takes the ends as the beginning and end of day, dawn and sunset, with part singled out from the whole as in the emphasized middle prayer in 2:238.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r8.anchor: قيل : المراد أول النهار وآخره ، وهما وقتا الصبح والمغرب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r9.claim: Another interpretation means the sun’s arc endpoints, including its midpoint at noon; 11:114 uses the ends of the day, and the two endpoints can frame the time of one prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p338/r9.anchor: وقيل : المراد طرف سير الشمس في قوس الأفق ، وهو بلوغ سيرها وسط الأفق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r10.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their accusations that he is a sorcerer, soothsayer, or liar, since their destruction is coming.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r10.anchor: ثم أمره تعالى بالصبر على أقوالهم إنه ساحر وإنه كاهن وإنه كذاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r1.claim: Most interpreters identify the times as five prayers: dawn before sunrise, afternoon before sunset, Isha in the night, and Maghrib and Dhuhr at the day's edges.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r1.anchor: الخمس قبل طلوع الشمس صلاة الصبح وقبل غروبها صلاة العصر ومن آناء الليل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r2.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r2.claim: Another group assigns Maghrib and Isha to the night and Dhuhr alone to the day's edges.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r2.anchor: وقالت فرقة آناء الليل المغرب والعشاء، وأطراف النهار الظهر وحدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r3.claim: The wording may instead refer to saying subhan Allah wa bihamdihi after dawn until the two rakas of duha and before sunset; a prophetic report promises forgiveness for seventy glorifications before sunset.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r3.anchor: ويحتمل اللفظ أن يراد قول سبحان الله وبحمده من بعد صلاة الصبح إلى ركعتي الضحى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r4.claim: The plural edges can reflect dual phrasing like your hearts, the generic recurrence of a day, or the two halves of daylight divided at noon; Ibn Furak notes the last analysis.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r4.anchor: وسمى الطرفين أطرافا على أحد وجهين إما على نحو فقد صغت قلوبكما

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r5.speaker: الهذلي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r5.claim: The poetic line uses ana for an hour of the night, supporting the explanation of anāʾ as times.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r5.anchor: والآناء جمع أنى وهي الساعة من الليل ومنه قول الهذلي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r6.speaker: فرقة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r6.claim: Another interpretation takes the verse as referring to voluntary prayers, including night prayers, the two pre-dawn rakas, and Maghrib.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r6.anchor: وقالت فرقة في الآية إشارة إلى نوافل، فمنها آناء الليل ومنها قبل طلوع الشمس

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r7.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r7.claim: The majority read tarḍa with fatḥa, so that the Prophet may be rewarded with what satisfies him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r7.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «لعلك ترضى» بفتح التاء أي لعلك تثاب على هذه الأعمال بما ترضى به

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r8.speaker: الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r8.claim: These readers use ḍamma on the tāʾ, meaning that the Prophet will be given what pleases him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p70/r8.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم «لعلك ترضى» أي لعلك تعطى ما يرضيك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r1.claim: The command to endure what they say lasts until God judged them; the later command to fight abrogated the permission simply to endure.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r1.anchor: أمر الله تعالى نبيه بالصبر على ما يسمع من أذاهم إلى أن يحكم الله فيهم ثم حكم فيهم بالقتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r2.claim: Glorifying with praise means prayer: before sunrise is dawn prayer and before sunset is afternoon prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r2.anchor: أي صل له بالحمد له والثناء عليه قبل طلوع الشمس يريد الفجر وقبل غروبها يعني العصر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r3.claim: One view takes the night prayers to be Maghrib and Isha.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r3.anchor: أحدها المغرب والعشاء رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r4.speaker: العوفي عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r4.claim: Another view makes them the middle of the night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r4.anchor: والثاني جوف الليل رواه العوفي عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r5.claim: A third view is the Isha prayer.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r5.anchor: والثالث العشاء قاله مجاهد وابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r6.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r6.claim: A fourth view takes this as the beginning, middle, and end of night.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r6.anchor: والرابع أول الليل وأوسطه وأخره قاله الحسن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r7.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r7.claim: Though the expression أطراف النهار is plural, it refers to two ends, like the dual example of two hearts in 66:4.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r7.anchor: قال الفراء إنما هم طرفان فخرجا مخرج الجمع

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r8.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r8.claim: One interpretation of the day's ends is the noon prayer, which lies at the edge of each half of the day.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r9.claim: Another interpretation is Maghrib and dawn, at the start and end of the day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r9.anchor: والثاني انها صلاة المغرب وصلاة الصبح قاله ابن زيد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r10.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r10.claim: A third interpretation includes dawn, noon, and afternoon prayers.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r10.anchor: والثالث أنها الفجر والظهر والعصر فعلى هذا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r11.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r11.claim: They read ترضى with fatḥa on tāʾ, meaning that the Prophet may be pleased with God's reward.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r11.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وابو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة وحفص عن عاصم ترضى بفتح التاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r12.speaker: الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r12.claim: They read ترضى with ḍamma on tāʾ: either the Prophet is pleased with what he receives or God is pleased with him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p333#3/r12.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم بضمها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r3.claim: The Prophet is consoled to endure their denials; glorifying God before sunrise and sunset means the dawn and afternoon prayers. In an authentic report, Jarir says the Prophet compared seeing God to seeing the full moon and urged guarding those prayers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r3.anchor: فإن استطعتم ألا تغلبوا على صلاة قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها، فافعلوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r4.claim: The Prophet said that no one who performs prayer before sunrise and before sunset will enter the Fire; Muslim transmits the report from Umara ibn Ruwayba.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r4.anchor: لن يلج النار أحد صلى قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r5.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says the lowest person in Paradise sees a kingdom stretching a thousand years, while the highest in rank sees God twice each day.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p325/r5.anchor: إن أدنى أهل الجنة منزلة من ينظر في ملكه مسيرة ألف سنة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r1.claim: The night intervals mean its hours and the night prayer; some instead interpret them as the sunset and night prayers. The day's ends correspond to the night intervals.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r1.anchor: وقوله: {ومن آناء الليل فسبح} أي: من ساعاته فتهجد به. وحمله بعضهم على المغرب والعشاء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r2.claim: The hope of contentment recalls God's promise to give until the Prophet is pleased in 93:5.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى} [الضحى: 5]

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r3.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r3.claim: In an authentic report, God asks the people of Paradise if they are satisfied; after they cite His unmatched gifts, He promises them His pleasure and says He will never be displeased with them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r3.anchor: أحل عليكم رضواني، فلا أسخط عليكم بعده أبدا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r4.speaker: النبي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r4.claim: Another report says that after people of Paradise recall that God whitened their faces, weighted their scales, saved them from the Fire, and admitted them to Paradise, the veil is lifted and seeing God proves a greater gift, called the increase.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p326/r4.anchor: فوالله ما أعطاهم خيرا من النظر إليه، وهي (5) الزيادة

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r3.speaker: الكسائي، أبو بكر عن عاصم
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r3.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr from Asim read ترضى with passive u-vowel; other readers use the active reading, in line with 93:5.
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r3.anchor: قرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم: ترضى بضم التاء

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r5.claim: Anaʾ al-layl are its hours; the singular has several forms, and the cited Hudhali line illustrates إني as a time word.
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r5.anchor: وآناء الليل: ساعاته وأوقاته، واحده: إنى، مثل معى وأمعاء

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r6.speaker: الهذلي
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r6.claim: The poet uses بكل إني for each portion of the night, demonstrating the singular form of آناء.

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r9.claim: أطراف is coordinated with قبل طلوع الشمس; its plural has three explanations: each day's two edges, a dual-like form like 'your hearts,' or the boundary shared by two halves.
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r9.anchor: ويقال: لم قال: (أطراف النهار) على الجمع؟ قلنا: فيه ثلاثة أقوال؟

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r1.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r1.claim: Al-Shafi'i permits combining prayers during travel or rain and says advancing all prayers is preferable.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r1.anchor: وقيل: في السفر والمطر، عن الشافعي، وقيل: في كل من كان مشغولا له عذر، عن الهادي

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r2.speaker: الهادي
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r2.claim: Al-Hadi permits combining when a person is occupied and has an excuse.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r2.anchor: في كل من كان مشغولا له عذر، عن الهادي

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r3.claim: One reported view permits combining in all circumstances; Abu Hanifa gives a more differentiated account of which prayers to advance.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r3.anchor: وقيل: في عموم الأحوال، واختلفوا، فقيل: التعجيل في جميع الصلوات أفضل، عن الشافعي

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r4.claim: Patience under enemies' abuse is good and may sometimes be obligatory; the sword-verse does not require abrogation because the rulings can coexist.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r4.anchor: ويدل قوله: فاصبر على أن الصبر على أذى الأعداء مما يحسن، وقد يجب في بعض الأحوال

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r5.claim: The patience command need not be treated as abrogated, since the two passages do not conflict.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r5.anchor: وقيل: لم تنسخه، ولا تنافي بينهما حتى يحمل على النسخ

JISHUMI:v7p4769/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r6.claim: لعلك ترضى indicates that worship is obligatory and done for reward, which is deserved for deeds.
JISHUMI:v7p4769/r6.anchor: ويدل قوله: (لعلك ترضى) أن العبادات تجب وتفعل لمكان الثواب

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r1.claim: بحمد ربك is circumstantial: glorify while praising Him.

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r2.claim: ومن آناء الليل attaches to the second سبح.

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r3.speaker: العامة
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r3.claim: The common accusative reading of وأطراف permits coordination with the syntactic position of ومن آناء الليل or with قبل.
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r3.anchor: وفيه وجهان أحدهما: أنه عطف على محل

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r4.speaker: الحسن وعيسى بن عمر
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r4.claim: Al-Hasan and Isa ibn Umar read وأطراف in the genitive, coordinated with آناء الليل.
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r4.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى بن عمر " وأطراف "

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r5.speaker: قيل
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r5.claim: The plural أطراف may stand for the dual طرفي in Hud, with a poetic parallel; alternatively it is a true plural meaning the hours.
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r5.anchor: فقيل: هو من وضع الجمع موضع التثنية

SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r6.speaker: الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r6.claim: Al-Kisai and Abu Bakr from Asim read ترضى in the passive; the other readers use the active, as in 93:5.
SAMIN-DURR:20:130/r6.anchor: قرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم ترضى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r1.claim: “With praise of your Lord” may be a circumstantial phrase: praise Him for enabling and helping you to pray.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r1.anchor: بحمد ربك } في موضع الحال ، أي : وأنت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r2.claim: Tasbih means prayer: dawn before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, night prayer, and prayers at the day’s edges.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r2.anchor: والمراد بالتسبيح الصلاة . أو على ظاهر قدم الفعل على الأوقات أولا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r3.claim: Alternatively, the order of time phrases and action conveys prayer at those times; night worship is especially meritorious for focus, quiet, solitude with God, effort and stronger fulfillment of duty, as 73:6 and 39:9 indicate.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r3.anchor: وذلك أن أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل ، لاجتماع القلب وهدو الرجل والخلو بالرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r4.claim: Night includes the late prayer, and the day’s edges include Maghrib and Fajr; their repetition marks special status, like the “middle prayer” in 2:238 for some exegetes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r4.anchor: وقد تناول التسبيح في آناء الليل صلاة العتمة ، وفي أطراف النهار صلاة المغرب وصلاة الفجر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r5.claim: “Edges of the day” is plural to avoid ambiguity; the dual in 11:114 gives added clarity, like the poetic example of two backs.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r5.anchor: قلت : الوجه أمن الإلباس ، وفي التثنية زيادة بيان . ونظير مجيء الأمرين في الآيتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r6.claim: A reading coordinates “the edges of the day” with “the hours of night.”
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r6.anchor: وقرىء : ( وأطراف النهار ) عطفا على آناء الليل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r7.claim: Laʿalla addresses the Prophet, expressing hope that remembrance at these times brings what satisfies him and gladdens his heart.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r7.anchor: ولعل للمخاطب ، أي : اذكر الله في هذه الأوقات ، طمعا ورجاء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p96#5/r8.claim: A reading makes the verb passive: that your Lord may satisfy you.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r7.claim: The command to endure concerns abuse and false accusations.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r8.claim: Before sunrise is dawn prayer, before sunset afternoon prayer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r9.claim: Night watches may mean prayer throughout the night.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r9.anchor: أحدهما : هي صلاة الليل كله , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r10.claim: Alternatively, the watches mean sunset and night prayers.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r11.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r11.claim: Day's endpoints may mean dawn prayer at the end of one half and start of the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r11.anchor: صلاة الفجر لأنها آخر النصف الأول , وأول النصف الثاني : قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r12.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r12.claim: Alternatively, they refer to voluntary prayer.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r13.speaker: عاصم والكسائي
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r13.claim: They read tardā with ḍamma on tāʾ: God may please the Prophet through honor or intercession.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p431/r13.anchor: وقرأ عاصم والكسائي { ترضى } بضم التاء يعني لعل الله يرضيك بكرامته , وقيل بالشفاعة

MUQATIL:20:130-131/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r1.claim: Be patient with their denial of the threatened punishment; tasbih here means prayer by God's command at the listed times, in hope of reward in the Hereafter.
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r1.anchor: { فاصبر على ما يقولون } من تكذيبهم إياك بالعذاب { وسبح بحمد ربك } يعنى صل بأمر ربك

MUQATIL:20:130-131/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r2.claim: Before sunrise is dawn; before sunset means noon and afternoon; night includes the sunset and evening prayers, and the day's edges are for prayer.
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r2.anchor: { قبل طلوع الشمس } يعنى الفجر { وقبل غروبها } يعنى الظهر والعصر { ومن آنآء الليل } يعنى المغرب والعشاء

MUQATIL:20:130-131/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r3.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r3.claim: Prayer was initially two cycles at dawn and evening; after the Ascension five prayers were imposed, two cycles each except sunset, then after migration all prayers were completed.
MUQATIL:20:130-131/r3.anchor: قال مقاتل: كانت الصلاة ركعتين بالغداة وركعتين بالعشي، فلما عرج بالنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فرضت عليه خمس صلوات

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r1.claim: Tasbīḥ here means prayer, offered while praising God for enabling and helping the worshipper.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r1.anchor: في موضع الحال وانت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r2.claim: Before sunrise is Fajr; before sunset comprises Ẓuhr and ʿAṣr, which fall in the latter half of daylight.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r2.anchor: ﴿ قبل طلوع الشمس ﴾ يعني صلاة الفجر

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r3.claim: The night hours include ʿIshāʾ; the day’s ends include Maghrib and Fajr, with Fajr repeated to mark the particular periods for prayer.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r3.anchor: وقد تناول التبسيح في آناء الليل صلاة العتمة وفي اطراف النهار صلاة المغرب

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r4.claim: “Ends of the day” is plural although there are two ends, and it is coordinated with “before”; the phrasing emphasizes those prayer times.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r4.anchor: وإنام جمع أطراف النهار وهما طرفان لا من الالباس وهو عطف على قبل

NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r5.claim: The hope may be that the worshipper becomes content and glad, or, in the readings of ʿAlī and Abū Bakr, that the Lord makes him content.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p72/r5.anchor: لعل المخاطب أي اذكر الله في هذه الأوقات رجاء أن تنال عند الله

QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r8.claim: The Prophet is commanded to endure their accusations that he is a sorcerer, soothsayer, or liar, knowing their punishment has a fixed time.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r8.anchor: أمره تعالى بالصبر على أقوالهم: إنه ساحر إنه كاهن إنه كذاب

QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r9.claim: Some say the patience command was abrogated by the fighting verse; others say it remains, since fighting did not annihilate all disbelievers.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r9.anchor: ثم قيل: هذا منسوخ بآية القتال. وقيل: ليس منسوخا

QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r10.speaker: أكثر المتأولين
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r10.claim: Most commentators take the prayer references as the five daily prayers: dawn before sunrise, afternoon before sunset, night prayer in the night hours, and Maghrib and noon at the day’s extremities.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r10.anchor: قال أكثر المتأولين: هذه إشارة إلى الصلوات الخمس

QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r11.claim: One explanation of day’s extremities counts the shared boundary at noon for both halves; Ibn Furak notes this analysis.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:128-130/r11.anchor: وقيل: النهار ينقسم قسمين فصلهما الزوال، ولكل قسم طرفان

QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r1.claim: Another explanation treats day as a generic recurring unit, so the plural extremities reflects each day having an end.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r1.anchor: وقيل: النهار للجنس فلكل يوم طرف، وهو إلى جمع لأنه يعود في كل نهار

QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r2.claim: Anāʾ al-layl means its hours; its singular has several forms, ini, inā, and anā.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r2.anchor: «وآناء الليل» ساعاته وواحد الآناء إني وإنى وأنى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r3.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r3.claim: Hasan says the command refers to voluntary prayer.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r3.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المراد بالآية صلاة التطوع قاله الحسن

QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r4.claim: With fatḥa on the tāʾ, tarḍā means that the Prophet may be rewarded until content; al-Kisaʾi and Abu Bakr from Asim read the passive with ḍamma, meaning given what pleases him.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:130/r4.anchor: } بفتح التاء أي لعلك تثاب على هذه الأعمال بما ترضى به

ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r2.claim: Tasbih before sunrise and sunset means dawn and evening; the night hours are its portions, and the day's ends include noon and afternoon.

ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p380/r3.claim: The source notes a recitation variant for لعلك ترضى.

RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r16.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r16.claim: Patience is commanded in response to whatever hurts the Prophet: insults such as sorcerer, madman, or poet; denial of his prophethood; or refusal to accept his call.
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r16.anchor: فيحتمل أن يكون ذلك قول بعضهم

RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r17.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r17.claim: The command encourages continued patience, calling people to God, and delivering the entrusted message despite their conduct.
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r17.anchor: فرغبه تعالى في الصبر وبعثه على الإدامة على الدعاء إلى الله تعالى وإبلاغ ما حمل من الرسالة

RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r18.speaker: الكلبي ومقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r18.claim: Al-Kalbi and Muqatil say the patience command was abrogated by the fighting verse.

RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r19.claim: The command to glorify with praise is comparable to the instruction to seek aid through patience and prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p114#2/r19.anchor: وهو نظير قوله : { واستعينوا بالصبر والصلواة }

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r1.claim: The phrase with your Lord's praise is circumstantial: the Prophet glorifies while praising God for enabling and assisting him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r1.anchor: في موضع الحال وأنت حامد لربك على أن وفقك للتسبيح

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r2.claim: Glorification follows the command to be patient because remembrance of God gives solace and rest; believers find no rest apart from meeting God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r2.anchor: إنما أمر عقيب الصبر بالتسبيح لأن ذكر الله تعالى يفيد السلوة والراحة

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r3.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r3.claim: Most commentators take glorification here to mean prayer and offer three accounts of how the prayer times are specified.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r3.anchor: فالأكثرون على أن المراد منه الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says the verse establishes exactly five prayers: dawn before sunrise, noon and afternoon before sunset, and sunset and night prayers during the night; the day-end phrase reinforces dawn and sunset.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r4.anchor: دخلت الصلوات الخمس فيه ، فقبل طلوع الشمس

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r5.claim: A second prayer reading includes the five obligatory prayers in the two daylight periods and treats the night watches and day ends as additional voluntary prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r5.anchor: أن الآية تدل على الصلوات الخمس وزيادة

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r6.claim: A third prayer reading identifies dawn, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, leaving the noon prayer outside the verse.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r6.anchor: أنها تدل على أقل من الخمس

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r7.claim: Razi judges the first interpretation, which includes exactly the five prayers, the strongest and best supported.

RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r8.claim: Abu Muslim says glorification may instead mean declaring God's transcendence and majesty at these times, not ritual prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r8.anchor: لا يبعد حمله على التنزيه والإجلال
