RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r9.claim: Razi says Abu Muslim's reading is closer to the apparent sense and context: after abuse and denial, the Prophet should proclaim God's transcendence and call people to Him at all times.
RAZI-FULL:v22p115/r9.anchor: وهذا القول أقرب إلى الظاهر وإلى ما تقدم ذكره

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r1.claim: Night is the best time for remembrance because people are quiet, movement and sensory activity cease, and worship then is harder for body and soul and so earns greater reward.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r1.anchor: أفضل الذكر ما كان بالليل لأن الجمعية فيه أكثر

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r2.claim: One answer to why the verse says ends of the day in plural is that the minimum plural can mean two.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r2.anchor: من الناس من قال أقل الجمع اثنان فسقط السؤال

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r3.claim: Another answer is that the two ends recur every day, so they are expressed in the plural.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r3.anchor: إنما جمع لأنه يتكرر في كل نهار ويعود

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r4.claim: One gloss of so that you may be pleased is a promise of elevated favor, like a sovereign telling a servant that service may bring him benefit.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r4.anchor: يا فلان اشتغل بالخدمة فلعلك تنتفع به

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r5.claim: A second gloss is that the Prophet may be pleased with the reward he receives.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r5.anchor: لعلك ترضى ما تنال من الثواب

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r6.claim: A third gloss is that he may be pleased with the intercession granted to him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r6.anchor: لعلك ترضى ما تنال من الشفاعة

RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r7.speaker: الكسائي وعاصم
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r7.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Asim read ترضى with a damma on the tāʾ; the meaning is unchanged, since God making the Prophet content is equivalent to being pleased with him.
RAZI-FULL:v22p116/r7.anchor: لعلك ترضى بضم التاء والمعنى لا يختلف

STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.speaker: some
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.claim: Ṭā Hā is Makkan; some classify verses 130–131 as Madinan, but their context suggests they are Makkan.
STUDYQURAN:20:intro/r1.anchor: which some consider to be Madinan (JJ)

ASAD-NOTES:20:129#n114/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:129#n114/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:129#n114/r1.claim: The phrase means at the sides or extremities of the day and is linked to 11:114.
ASAD-NOTES:20:129#n114/r1.anchor: See in this connection also 11:114 and the corresponding note 145

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r1.speaker: JJ, Q
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r1.claim: The references to before sunrise and sunset denote the dawn and late-afternoon prayers.

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r2.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r2.claim: The hours of night refer to the night prayer.
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r2.anchor: in the hours of the night refers to the night prayer (ʿishāʾ; Q)

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r3.claim: The day's ends refer to the midday and sunset prayers: midday closes the first part of the day and begins the second, while sunset closes the second part.
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r3.anchor: the sunset prayer stands at the end of the second part of the day (Q)

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r4.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r4.claim: Glorifying God at these times brings contentment with the reward God gives.
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r4.anchor: one will be content with the reward that will be given by God (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r5.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r5.claim: Alternatively, the phrase can mean becoming generally content with whatever God gives in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r5.anchor: It can also mean that one will become generally content with whatever is given by God in the life of this world.

STUDYQURAN:20:130/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r6.speaker: Aj
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r6.claim: Spiritually, seekers should be patient, devoted solely to their Master, turn from sin and concern with others' opinions, and persist in remembrance until selfhood vanishes in divine Presence and they witness the Beloved.
STUDYQURAN:20:130/r6.anchor: they will become content in witnessing the Beloved (Aj)

TAB-FULL:v16p207/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p207/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p207/r1.claim: A prior decree and appointed term prevent the people from being destroyed before their allotted time; lāzim is the verbal noun of lāzama, meaning something that would have adhered.
TAB-FULL:v16p207/r1.anchor: يخترمه قبل بلوغه أجله {وأجل مسمى} [الأنعام: 2] يقول: ووقت مسمى

TAB-FULL:v16p209/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r1.claim: The Prophet should endure his people’s accusations that he is a sorcerer, madman, poet, and similar insults.
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r1.anchor: فاصبر يا محمد على ما يقول هؤلاء المكذبون بآيات الله من قومك لك إنك ساحر

TAB-FULL:v16p209/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r2.claim: سبح بحمد ربك means pray while praising your Lord; the construction makes God’s praise the object, as in the phrase I admire Zayd’s striking, meaning my striking Zayd.
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r2.anchor: والمعنى: بحمدك ربك، كما تقول: أعجبني ضرب زيد

TAB-FULL:v16p209/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r3.claim: Before sunrise means the dawn prayer, before sunset the afternoon prayer, and the night intervals refer to the evening prayer after part of the night has passed.
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r3.anchor: وذلك صلاة الصبح {وقبل غروبها} [طه: 130] وهي العصر

TAB-FULL:v16p209/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r4.claim: Ānāʾ means the hours or periods of night, with singular inī; an unnamed line by al-Munkhil al-Saʿdī illustrates the word’s use for a night period.
TAB-FULL:v16p209/r4.anchor: وهي ساعات الليل، واحدها: إني، على تقدير حمل

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r1.claim: The ends of the day refer to noon and sunset prayers: noon lies at the meeting of the day's two ends, while sunset is its third end and time for Maghrib.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r1.anchor: كما قيل {صغت قلوبكما} [التحريم: 4] فجمع، والمراد: قلبان

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the prayers before sunrise and sunset as the prescribed prayers.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r2.anchor: عن عاصم، عن ابن أبي زيد، عن ابن عباس، {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس وقبل غروبها} [طه: 130] قال: الصلاة المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r3.speaker: جرير بن عبد الله عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r3.claim: The Prophet compared believers' sight of God to seeing the full moon and urged them to guard the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r3.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله، قال: كنا جلوسا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، فرأى القمر ليلة البدر

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r4.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r4.claim: Ibn Jurayj identifies the prayer before sunset as Asr and the day-end prayers as prescribed prayers.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r4.anchor: قال ابن جريج: العصر، وأطراف النهار قال: المكتوبة

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r5.claim: Qatada maps the times to Fajr before sunrise, Asr before sunset, Maghrib and Isha at night, and Dhuhr at the day's ends.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {وسبح بحمد ربك قبل طلوع الشمس} [طه: 130] قال: هي صلاة الفجر

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd identifies the night time as Isha and the ends of the day as Maghrib and Fajr.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r6.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله {ومن آناء الليل فسبح وأطراف النهار} [طه: 130] قال: من آناء الليل: العتمة

TAB-FULL:v16p210/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r7.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r7.claim: The accusative in “and the ends of the day” coordinates with “before sunrise,” yielding worship at the end of night and at the daytime ends.
TAB-FULL:v16p210/r7.anchor: ونصب قوله {وأطراف النهار} [طه: 130] عطفا على قوله {قبل طلوع الشمس} [طه: 130] لأن معنى ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p212/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets the night times as prayer throughout the whole night.
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r1.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس {ومن آناء الليل} [طه: 130] قال: المصلى من الليل كله

TAB-FULL:v16p212/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r2.claim: Al-Hasan explains the night times as its beginning, middle, and end.
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r2.anchor: سمعت الحسن، قرأ: {ومن آناء الليل} [طه: 130] قال: من أوله، وأوسطه، وآخره

TAB-FULL:v16p212/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the night times with the middle of the night.
TAB-FULL:v16p212/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {ومن آناء الليل فسبح} [طه: 130] قال: آناء الليل: جوف الليل

TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r1.claim: Most Medinan and Iraqi readers read “that you may be pleased” with an open tāʾ; ʿĀṣim, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read it with a ḍamma.
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r1.anchor: إلى معنى: إن الله يعطيك، حتى ترضى عطيته وثوابه إياك

TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r2.claim: On the open-tāʾ reading, Ibn Zayd says the verse means that the Prophet will be pleased with God's reward.
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {لعلك ترضى} [طه: 130] قال: الثواب، ترضى بما يثيبك الله على ذلك

TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r3.speaker: ابن جريج
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r3.claim: Ibn Jurayj glosses the open-tāʾ reading as being pleased with what one is given.
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r3.anchor: عن ابن جريج، {لعلك ترضى} [طه: 130] قال: بما تعطى

TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r4.claim: The ḍamma reading means that God may make the Prophet content with his worship and obedience.
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r4.anchor: وجهوا معنى الكلام إلى لعل الله يرضيك من عبادتك إياه، وطاعتك له

TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r5.claim: Both established readings are widespread and agree in meaning: when God pleases someone, that person is pleased, so either reading is correct.
TAB-FULL:v16p212#2/r5.anchor: وهما قراءتان مستفيضتان في قراءة الأمصار، متفقتا المعنى، غير مختلفتيه

TABATABAI:20:130/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130/r5.claim: Because God delays punishment for what people say, the Prophet should patiently accept God's decree, reject their shirk, and praise God for the effects of that decree.
TABATABAI:20:130/r5.anchor: إذا كان من قضاء الله أن يؤخر عذابهم ولا يعاجلهم بالانتقام على ما يقولون فلا يبقى لك إلا أن تصبر راضيا على ما قضاه الله

TABATABAI:20:130/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130/r6.claim: Glorification rejects attributing evil to God, while praise recognizes that events permitted by Him are beautiful in their wider benefits and ordering of the world.
TABATABAI:20:130/r6.anchor: لها نسبة إلى فواعلها وليست إلا سيئة يجب تنزيهه تعالى عنها ولها نسبة بالإذن إليه تعالى وهي بهذه النسبة جميلة

TABATABAI:20:130/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130/r7.claim: The phrases before sunrise and before sunset are temporal modifiers of the command to glorify God.
TABATABAI:20:130/r7.anchor: ظرفان متعلقان بقوله { وسبح بحمد ربك }

TABATABAI:20:130/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130/r8.claim: “Some of the night times” uses a partitive min; anāʾ is the plural of inā or inw, meaning a time, and the phrase specifies when to glorify.
TABATABAI:20:130/r8.anchor: والآناء على أفعال جمع إني أو إنو بكسر الهمزة

TABATABAI:20:130/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130/r9.claim: The fronted phrase “and Me alone fear” in 2:40 has a comparable construction.

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r1.claim: “The edges of the day” is accusative after an omitted preposition and coordinated with the phrase about night; its implied sense is glorify during the day's edges.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r1.anchor: منصوب بنزع الخافض على ما ذكروا

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r2.claim: The verse does not lexically require obligatory prayers; some exegetes read general glorification, while most follow early authorities such as Qatada in identifying prayer.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r2.anchor: وما ذكر في الآية من التسبيح مطلق

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r3.claim: The prayer interpretation maps before sunrise to dawn, before sunset to afternoon, night times to sunset and night prayers, and day edges to noon.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r3.anchor: وقوله { ومن آناء الليل } صلاتا المغرب والعشاء

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r4.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r4.claim: To make noon fall at the day’s edges, interpreters divide daytime into halves and treat noon as a boundary of both halves.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r4.anchor: لو نصف النهار حصل نصفان الأول والأخير وصلاة الظهر في الجزء الأول من النصف الثاني فهي في طرف النصف الأول

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r5.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r5.claim: The plural “edges” is explained either as a plural used for two or by taking day generically, with two edges for every day.

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r6.claim: Al-Tabataba'i calls the explanations that make midday an edge strained and contrary to ordinary understanding and conversational usage.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r6.anchor: يأبى أن يسمي وسط النهار أطراف النهار

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r7.claim: A broader reading takes glorification as inward remembrance, spoken praise, or both, and identifies the times as dawn, afternoon, and night.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r7.anchor: وأما من قال إن المراد بالتسبيح والتحميد غير الفرائض من مطلق التسبيح والحمد إما بتذكر تنزيهه والثناء عليه تعالى قلبا وإما بقول مثل سبحان الله

TABATABAI:20:130#2/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r8.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r8.claim: On the general-remembrance reading, dawn and afternoon are repeated at the day edges; some accept repetition for emphasis, while others include midday too.
TABATABAI:20:130#2/r8.anchor: وأما لزوم التكرار بذكر تسبيح الصبح والعصر مرتين فقد التزم به بعضهم قائلا أن ذلك للتأكيد

TABATABAI:20:130#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r1.claim: The alternative general-remembrance reading faces the same problem of explaining “edges,” since neither dawn and afternoon nor midday naturally matches the plural phrase.
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r1.anchor: والإشكال كله ناش من ناحية قوله

TABATABAI:20:130#3/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r2.claim: Al-Tabataba'i proposes that “the edges of the day” is a comitative object, with the time preposition implicit, and refers to the broad intervals before sunrise and sunset.

TABATABAI:20:130#3/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r3.claim: Those broad intervals contain multiple parts, each an edge relative to midday, just as the early and late portions of a day can be expressed in both singular and plural.
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r3.anchor: بالنظر إلى كونهما وقتين ذوي سعة لكل منهما أجزاء كل جزء منها طرف بالنسبة إلى وسط النهار

TABATABAI:20:130#3/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r4.claim: The time relation is implicit on both sides: night is introduced by partitive min, while “day edges” likewise means alongside the times when glorification occurs.
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r4.anchor: وهو مدخول من ولا معنى لتقدير في معه

TABATABAI:20:130#3/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r5.claim: Under the non-prayer reading, the command covers parts of the day's beginning, end, and night without repeated times or a plural-used-for-two problem.
TABATABAI:20:130#3/r5.anchor: كان المراد التسبيح في أجزاء من أول النهار وأجزاء من آخره وأجزاء من الليل بمعية أجزاء أول النهار وآخره ولم يلزم محذور التكرار

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r1.claim: On the prayer reading, the verse commands dawn, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, but not noon; Hud 11:114 gives a similar four-prayer pattern.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r1.anchor: وأقم الصلاة طرفي النهار وزلفا من الليل

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r2.claim: Since the suras of Ta-Ha and Hud preceded the post-Ascension al-Isra, the daily prayers may then have been four; five were later instituted, as in 17:78.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r2.anchor: الفرائض اليومية إنما شرعت خمسا في المعراج كما ذكرت في سورة الإسراء النازلة بعد المعراج خمسا في قوله أقم الصلاة لدلوك الشمس إلى غسق الليل وقرآن الفجر

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r3.claim: In context, “so that you may be satisfied” means becoming content with God's decree, much like the instruction to seek help through patience and prayer.

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r4.claim: Persistent glorification and praise deepen familiarity with God and awareness of the beauty of His acts, quieting distractions and producing contentment in the soul.
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r4.anchor: إدامة ذكره بالتسبيح والتحميد تورث الرضا بقضائه

TABATABAI:20:130-131/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r5.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:20:130-131/r5.claim: Other interpretations say the satisfaction is through intercession and a high rank with God, or through all promises of victory, religious honor, intercession, and Paradise.

TABRISI:20:130/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:130/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to endure their denials and insults and to praise God in prayer and thanksgiving.
TABRISI:20:130/r1.anchor: { فاصبر على ما يقولون } من تكذيبك وأذاهم إياك

TABRISI:20:130/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:130/r2.claim: ‘Before sunrise’ means the dawn prayer and ‘before sunset’ the afternoon prayer.
TABRISI:20:130/r2.anchor: يعني صلاة الفجر { وقبل غروبها } يعني صلاة العصر

TABRISI:20:130/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:20:130/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas takes the night hours to mean the whole night prayer; another view specifies the start of night, Maghrib and the later evening prayer.
TABRISI:20:130/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي صلاة الليل كله

TABRISI:20:130/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r4.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:20:130/r4.claim: Qatada and al-Jubbaʾi interpret the day's two ends as the noon prayer, since noon borders both the first and second halves of the day.

TABRISI:20:130/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:130/r5.claim: If the command is taken literally rather than as prescribed prayer times, it asks for continuous praise and glorification throughout all hours.
TABRISI:20:130/r5.anchor: ومن حمل التسبيح على الظاهر قال أراد بذلك المداومة

TABRISI:20:130/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:130/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:130/r6.claim: The Prophet's satisfaction is explained either as intercession and exalted rank or as all God's promises of worldly victory and honor plus intercession and Paradise in the hereafter.
TABRISI:20:130/r6.anchor: وقيل: بجميع ما وعدك الله به من النصر وإعزاز الدين

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to endure what people say until God rules; then He decreed their killing, ending the command to endure their abuse.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r1.anchor: أمره بالصبر إلى أن يحكم الله، ثم حكم فيهم بالقتل، فنسخ الصبر على ما يسمع من أذاهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r2.claim: “Glorify with praise” means perform prayer while praising and extolling God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r2.anchor: {وسبح بحمد ربك} صل لله بالحمد له والثناء عليه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r3.claim: Before sunrise refers to dawn prayer; before sunset refers to afternoon prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r3.anchor: {قبل طلوع الشمس} يريد: الفجر {وقبل غروبها} يريد: العصر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r4.claim: “Hours of the night” means its times; the singular forms and two poetic lines illustrate the word's usage.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r4.anchor: ساعاته واحدها إني مثل: نحي وأنحاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r5.speaker: الأعشى
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r5.claim: Al-Asha's line uses ini for a span or time of night.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the early night prayers as Maghrib and Isha.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد أول الليل المغرب والعشاء)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r7.speaker: ابن عباس رواية عطاء، مجاهد، قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r7.claim: They identify “the edges of the day” as the noon prayer; noon is the boundary between the day's two halves, and a dual can be called a plural.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r7.anchor: {فسبح وأطراف النهار} يريد: الظهر. هذا الذي ذكرنا في تفسير هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r8.claim: Al-Farra gives the same interpretation of “the edges of the day” as noon prayer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r8.anchor: وهذا قول الفراء في هذه الآية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r9.speaker: أبو العباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r9.claim: Abu al-Abbas says the plural refers to the two edges recurring each day.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r9.anchor: جمع الطرفين؛ لأنه يلزم في كل نهار يعود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r10.speaker: بعض المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r10.claim: Some exegetes take the edges to mean morning and evening, inferred from the preceding dawn and sunset phrases.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r10.anchor: ومن المفسرين من حمل أطراف النهار على: الغدوة والعشية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r11.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p557/r11.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the edges of the day are its hours.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r1.claim: “So that you may be pleased” means God guarantees the Prophet's reward and final return.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد: الثواب # والمعاد واجبا من الله لك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r2.claim: The verb has readings with a damma or fatha on its initial ta; the open reading is supported by the promise that God will give until the Prophet is satisfied.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r2.anchor: وفيه قراءتان: ضم التاء وفتحها (¬2). فمن فتح التاء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r3.claim: With the damma reading, the meaning can be that the Prophet is pleased by performing God's approved commands or by receiving a high rank.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r3.anchor: ويكون المعنى لعلك ترضى بفعل ما أمرك به من الأفعال التي يرضاها الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r4.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r4.claim: Abu Ubayd chooses the damma reading because it allows both being granted contentment and God's being pleased, supported by the description of Moses as pleasing to his Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p558/r4.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد هذه القراءة لاحتمالها معنيين أحدهما: ترضى: تعطى الرضى، والآخر: يرضاك الله

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r6.claim: The prayers are dawn, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers, plus noon prayer in the latter part of the day; the singular “side” is expressed by a plural form, and the Prophet hopes for reward at resurrection.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r6.anchor: صلاة الفجر { وقبل غروبها } صلاة العصر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r1.claim: The Prophet is told to endure claims that he is a sorcerer, poet, madman, liar, and soothsayer.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r1.anchor: قوله: {فاصبر على ما يقولون} [طه: 130] من قولهم لك: إنك ساحر، وإنك شاعر، وإنك مجنون، وإنك كاذب، وإنك كاهن.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r2.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r2.claim: Qatāda identifies prayer before sunrise as the dawn prayer, and before sunset as noon and afternoon prayers; night portions are Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ or the hours of night.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r2.anchor: نا سعيد، عن قتادة قال: صلاة الصبح. {وقبل غروبها} [طه: 130] الظهر والعصر.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r3.speaker: عمرو
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r3.claim: ʿAmr explains the phrase about the ends of the day; al-Hasan takes it as voluntary prayer, while Ibn ʿAbbās says before sunrise and sunset means the prescribed prayers.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي: {ومن آناء الليل} [طه: 130] يعني: ومن ساعات الليل.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r4.speaker: رسول الله
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r4.claim: The Prophet tells the companions they will see their Lord as clearly as the full moon, and urges them not to miss the two prayers before sunrise and sunset, citing this verse.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p292/r4.anchor: عن جرير بن عبد الله قال: كنا عند رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليلة البدر فقال لنا:

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r2.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r2.claim: The Prophet will be satisfied in the Hereafter with the reward for his deeds; al-Hasan says he surely will be satisfied.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p294/r2.anchor: قوله: {لعلك ترضى} [طه: 130] لكي ترضى في الآخرة ثواب عملك. وقال الحسن: لعلك أي فإنك سترضى ثواب عملك في الآخرة.

ELMALILI:20:129-135/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r2.claim: The prayer instructions here set out all of the prayer times.
ELMALILI:20:129-135/r2.anchor: Burada da namaz vakitleri tamamıyla gösterilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.claim: The surah closes with encouragement for the Prophet and believers facing pressure: punishment awaits its divinely set time, so believers should endure, worship steadily, and keep striving; this work benefits them, and a blessed future belongs to the God-conscious.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r1.anchor: müminlerin İslâm mesajının hedefine ulaşması için bu tür beklentilere bel bağlamak yerine karşılaştıkları zorluklara katlanmaları, sürekli bir ibadet bilinci ve disiplini içinde mücadeleye devam etmeleri istenmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r3.speaker: tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r3.claim: Some commentaries try to show that verse 130 refers to the five daily prayers.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r3.anchor: Tefsirlerde 130. âyette beş vakit namazın kastedildiğini ispatlamaya çalışan yorumlar yer almakla beraber

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r4.claim: Because five daily prayers were not yet obligatory when the surah was revealed, the verse primarily urges continual glorification of God in thought, word, and action, bringing spiritual contentment and peace.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r4.anchor: bu sûrenin indiği dönemde henüz beş vakit namaz farz kılınmadığına göre– burada asıl amacın müminleri Allah’ı tesbih etmeye

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.speaker: Derveze
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.claim: Although reports place verses 130–131 in Medina, the author doubts this, especially because their style is Meccan.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:20:129/r7.anchor: bunların Medine’de indiğine dair rivayeti tereddütle karşılamak gerekir; özellikle üslûp açısından bunların Mekkî âyet özelliği taşıdığı görülmektedir

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p65/r4.claim: He should endure sarcastic remarks patiently and cling to prayer to attain patience; those demanding punishment should be directed to local history, and he should not pursue the wealthy to make them believe.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p83/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p83/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p83/r2.claim: The Prophet is told to endure his opponents' words and be diligent in prayer; prayer most effectively implants the belief that events occur by God's will for the greater good.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p83/r2.anchor: The greatest and most effective means to fully implant this belief in one’s mind is the prayer.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r1.claim: The Prophet's practice crystallizes the prayer timings.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r1.anchor: The Prophet (sws) has crystallized these timings through his own practice.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r2.claim: The Prophet is the Qur'an's teacher as well as its reciter.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r3.claim: Prayer is stressed as a means of acquiring perseverance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r3.anchor: the prayer is stressed upon as a means to acquire perseverance.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r4.claim: Difficult circumstances require diligence in optional prayers as well as obligatory ones.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r4.anchor: it is not merely the obligatory prayers which are needed

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r5.claim: The day's margins refer to chāsht, ẓuhr, and maghrib; ẓuhr is also a boundary because it divides the day in two.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r5.anchor: Deliberation shows that ẓuhr too is at the boundary since the day is divided into two by it.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r6.claim: The verse refutes the claim that Qur'anic prayer times are absent: it mentions obligatory prayer and also tahajjud and ishrāq.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r6.anchor: This verse clearly negates the view of those people who claim that the timings

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r7.claim: The Prophet delineates each prayer's details, including its extent and limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r7.anchor: it was his task to delineate all these details

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r8.claim: In the difficult phase of the truth's struggle with evil, prayer equips the Prophet and the ummah to persevere and merit God's help.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r8.anchor: the struggle between truth and evil

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r9.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r9.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r9.claim: In individual or collective hardship, tahajjud and ishrāq should also be maintained, although they are optional in ordinary circumstances; Islahi says this is corroborated by Qur'an, prophetic sayings, and righteous practice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r9.anchor: in challenging and difficult circumstances, whether they are individual or collective, these prayers must be adhered to as well

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r10.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r10.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r10.claim: The closing phrase promises that persistence and prayer will bring the Prophet abundant success in this world and the next; the phrase is compared with al-Ḍuḥā 93:5.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r10.anchor: In verse 5 of S ūrah al-Ḍuḥā, it is similarly said

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r11.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r11.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r11.claim: The prayers contain all the Prophet needs, so he need not look to anyone else for support.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p84/r11.anchor: and there is no need for him to look up to anyone else.

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r1.claim: The excerpt opens with an unattributed exhortation to beautify Quran recitation with one's voice; it gives no chain or grading here.

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r2.claim: Al-Razi holds that confusing ḍād with ẓāʾ does not invalidate prayer: they share voicing, frication and emphatic articulation, and softened ḍād approaches ẓāʾ, making distinction difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r2.anchor: المختار عندنا أن اشتباه الضاد بالظاء لا يبطل الصلاة ويدل على أن المشابهة حاصلة بينهما جدا

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r3.claim: Because no one is reported to have asked the Prophet or Companions about distinguishing these letters, even after non-Arabs entered Islam, the distinction is not an obligation.
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r3.anchor: لو كان هذا الفرق معتبرا لوقع السؤال عنه في زمان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وفي أزمنة الصحابة

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r4.claim: The Prophet is quoted saying that he is the most eloquent of those who pronounce ḍād, supporting the claim that its articulation is distinctive to Arabs.

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r5.claim: Scholars differ over whether emphatic lām is an eloquent dialect; even if accepted, they agree it cannot be emphatic when preceded by kasra because the transition is too difficult.
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r5.anchor: اختلفوا في أن اللام المغلظة هل هي من اللغات الفصيحة أم لا

RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r6.claim: Shādhdh readings such as kasra on dāl in al-ḥamdu or ḍamma on lām in lillāh are forbidden in prayer: a Quranic reading would have been mass-transmitted; outside prayer al-Razi suspends that proof, leaving the prayer prohibition in force.
RAZI-FULL:v1p60/r6.anchor: اتفقوا على أنه لا يجوز في الصلاة قراءة القرآن بالوجوه الشاذة مثل قولهم الحمد لله بكسر الدال من الحمد أو بضم اللام من لله

BURHAN:v2p134/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p134/r3.speaker: خديجة
BURHAN:v2p134/r3.claim: Khadīja reassured the Prophet at the start of revelation that God would never disgrace him because he maintained kinship ties.
BURHAN:v2p134/r3.anchor: وقول خديجة والله لا يخزيك الله أبدا إنك لتصل الرحم

BURHAN:v2p134/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p134/r5.speaker: أصحاب الغار
BURHAN:v2p134/r5.claim: The three people trapped in the cave advised one another to pray to God by each person’s best deed, hoping for release.
BURHAN:v2p134/r5.anchor: وفى هذا بين صلى الله عليه وسلم أصحاب الغار الثلاثة إذ قال بعضهم لبعض ليدع كل واحد

BURHAN:v4p396/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p396/r1.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p396/r1.claim: Ibn Mālik treats the hadith’s ‘there is no prayer more burdensome’ as evidence that ‘laysa’ can negate the entire genus, not merely one instance.
BURHAN:v4p396/r1.anchor: غير ابن مالك في كتاب شواهد التوضيح فقال في قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم ليس صلاة اثقل على المنافقين

BURHAN:v4p396/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p396/r7.speaker: السهيلي
BURHAN:v4p396/r7.claim: Al-Suhaylī rejects the claim that relative ‘mā’ simply equals ‘alladhī’: ‘mā’ is more ambiguous and can refer even to what does not exist.
BURHAN:v4p396/r7.anchor: وقال السهيلي كذا يقول النحويون انها بمعنى الذي مطلقا وليس كذلك بل بينهما تخالف

ITQAN:v1p49/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.speaker: أبو رافع
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.claim: Al-Suyuti argues for another Medinan exception in Ta-Ha: Abu Rafiʿ reports that a Jewish lender demanded collateral for a loan of flour, after which the Prophet said he was trustworthy in heaven and earth and the verse forbidding coveting worldly provision was revealed.
ITQAN:v1p49/r8.anchor: أخرج البزار وأبو يعلى عن أبي رافع قال أضاف النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ضيفا فأرسلني إلى رجل من اليهود

ITQAN:v1p267/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r1.speaker: كثير من الفريقين
ITQAN:v1p267/r1.claim: Some authorities count sixteen articulation points, omitting the oral cavity and assigning alif, long wāw, and yāʾ elsewhere.
ITQAN:v1p267/r1.anchor: وقال كثير من الفريقين ستة عشر فأسقطوا مخرج الحروف الجوفية وهي حروف المد واللين

ITQAN:v1p267/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r2.speaker: قوم
ITQAN:v1p267/r2.claim: Another group counts fourteen points by combining nūn, lām, and rāʾ at one point.
ITQAN:v1p267/r2.anchor: وقال قوم أربعة عشر فأسقطوا مخرج النون واللام والراء وجعلوها من مخرج واحد

ITQAN:v1p267/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r3.speaker: ابن الحاجب
ITQAN:v1p267/r3.claim: Ibn al-Ḥājib treats these counts as approximations, since every letter has its own distinct articulation point.
ITQAN:v1p267/r3.anchor: قال ابن الحاجب وكل ذلك تقريب وإلا فلكل حرف مخرج على حدة

ITQAN:v1p267/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r4.speaker: القراء
ITQAN:v1p267/r4.claim: Reciters identify a letter's precise articulation by preceding it with hamzat al-waṣl and pronouncing it still or doubled while observing its qualities.
ITQAN:v1p267/r4.anchor: قال القراء واختيار مخرج الحرف محققا أن تلفظ بهمزة الوصل وتأتي بالحرف بعده ساكنا أو مشددا

ITQAN:v1p267/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r5.claim: The oral cavity articulates long alif, wāw, and yāʾ when each follows a matching vowel.
ITQAN:v1p267/r5.anchor: المخرج الأول الجوف للألف والواو والياء الساكنتين بعد حركة تجانسهما

ITQAN:v1p267/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r6.claim: The deepest throat articulates hamza and hāʾ.

ITQAN:v1p267/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r7.claim: The middle throat articulates ʿayn and unpointed ḥāʾ.

ITQAN:v1p267/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r8.claim: The throat's nearest part to the mouth articulates ghayn and khāʾ.

ITQAN:v1p267/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r9.claim: The back of the tongue against the palate articulates qāf.
ITQAN:v1p267/r9.anchor: الخامس أقصى اللسان مما يلي الحلق وما فوقه من الحنك للقاف

ITQAN:v1p267/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r10.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r10.claim: Kāf comes from slightly below the qāf articulation, against the adjacent palate.
ITQAN:v1p267/r10.anchor: السادس أقصاه من أسفل مخرج القاف قليلا وما يليه من الحنك للكاف

ITQAN:v1p267/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r11.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r11.claim: The middle tongue against the middle palate articulates jīm, shīn, and non-long yāʾ.
ITQAN:v1p267/r11.anchor: السابع وسطه بينه وبين وسط الحنك للجيم والشين والياء

ITQAN:v1p267/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r12.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r12.claim: Ḍād comes from the tongue's edge against the molars, usually on the left, though the right side is also reported.
ITQAN:v1p267/r12.anchor: الثامن للضاد المعجمة من أول حافة اللسان وما يليه من الأضراس من الجانب الأيسر وقيل الأيمن

ITQAN:v1p267/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r13.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r13.claim: Lām comes along the tongue's edge from its front to its tip, against the upper palate.
ITQAN:v1p267/r13.anchor: التاسع اللام من حافة اللسان من أدناها إلى منتهى طرفه وما بينها وبين ما يليها من الحنك الأعلى

ITQAN:v1p267/r14.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r14.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r14.claim: Nūn comes from the tongue tip, slightly below the lām articulation.
ITQAN:v1p267/r14.anchor: العاشر للنون من طرفه أسفل اللام قليلا

ITQAN:v1p267/r15.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r15.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r15.claim: Rāʾ shares nūn's point but is farther back on the tongue.
ITQAN:v1p267/r15.anchor: الحادي عشر للراء من مخرج النون لكنها أدخل في ظهر اللسان

ITQAN:v1p267/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r16.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r16.claim: Ṭāʾ, dāl, and tāʾ come from the tongue tip against the roots of the upper incisors.
ITQAN:v1p267/r16.anchor: الثاني عشر للطاء والدال والتاء من طرف اللسان وأصول الثنايا العليا مصعدا إلى جهة الحنك

ITQAN:v1p267/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r17.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r17.claim: Ṣād, sīn, and zāy are sibilants articulated between the tongue tip and the lower incisors.
ITQAN:v1p267/r17.anchor: الثالث عشر الحرف الصفير والصاد والسين والزاي من بين طرف اللسان وفويق الثنايا السفلى

ITQAN:v1p267/r18.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r18.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r18.claim: Ẓāʾ, thāʾ, and dhāl come between the tongue tip and the upper incisor edges.
ITQAN:v1p267/r18.anchor: الرابع عشر للظاء والثاء والذال من بين طرفه وأطراف الثنايا العليا

ITQAN:v1p267/r19.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r19.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r19.claim: Fāʾ comes from the inside of the lower lip against the upper incisors.
ITQAN:v1p267/r19.anchor: الخامس عشر للفاء من باطن الشفة السفلى وأطراف الثنايا العليا

ITQAN:v1p267/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r20.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r20.claim: Bāʾ, mīm, and non-long wāw come from the meeting of the two lips.
ITQAN:v1p267/r20.anchor: السادس عشر للباء والميم والواو غير المدية بين الشفتين

ITQAN:v1p267/r21.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p267/r21.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p267/r21.claim: The nasal cavity is the point for nasalization in assimilation and for still nūn and mīm.
ITQAN:v1p267/r21.anchor: السابع عشر الخيشوم للغنة في الإدغام والنون والميم الساكنة

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r1.claim: In ‘your gift did not imitate the cloud; it fevered it, so its rain is sweat,’ an underlying comparison is transformed into an imaginative image beyond ordinary simile.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r1.anchor: لأنه وإن كان أصله التشبيه من حيث يشبه الجواد بالغيث فإنه وضع المعنى وضعا وصوره في صورة خرج معها إلى ما لا أصل له في التشبيه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r2.claim: Another example imagines the gardens’ fragrance as a perfume bestowed by the buried dead, rather than as their own scent.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r2.anchor: وما ريح الرياض لها ولكن كساها دفنهم في التراب طيبا

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r3.speaker: أبو العباس الضبي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Ḍabbī says the setting sun turns yellow from fear of separation, intensifying the pain of parting through an invented cause.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r3.anchor: ومن لطيف هذا النوع قول أبي العباس الضبي

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r4.speaker: الشبلي
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r4.claim: The verse about a cut vine branch weeping is attributed to al-Shiblī’s recitation; a related explanation that the setting sun fears separation is also attributed to a Sufi, and Abū al-Baʾs is said to have adapted it.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r4.anchor: وهو منسوب إلى إنشاد الشبلي ويقال أيضا إن أبا البأس أخذ معناه في بيته

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r5.claim: Al-Ṣūlī’s wind really blows the lover’s cloak over his face, but the poet invents jealousy as its motive; an actual action is given a fictional cause.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r5.anchor: وذلك أن الريح إذا كان وجهها نحو الوجه فواجب في طباعها أن ترد الرداء عليه

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r6.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r6.claim: Ibn Wahb instead attributes an unreal act of hostility to time and supplies love as its cause; this differs from inventing a motive for the wind’s real physical action.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p242/r6.anchor: وحاربني فيه ريب الزمان كأن الزمان له عاشق

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r1.claim: The line about the sun as separation’s setting and the moon as estrangement’s eclipse approaches metaphor: restoring an explicit comparison would require breaking and recasting its syntax.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r1.anchor: فهو اقرب إلى أن تسمية إستعارة لأنه قد غمض تقدير حرف التشبيه فيه إذ لا تصل إلى الكاف حتى تبطل بنية الكلام

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r2.claim: When descriptive details make an explicit comparison contradictory, the expression approaches metaphor: the hero cannot be both likened to a lion or death and positioned above them; the cloud and sea examples use the same paradox.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p286/r2.anchor: لا سبيل لك إلى أن تقول هو كالأسد وهو كالموت لما يكون في ذلك من التناقض

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r1.claim: A sentence’s meaning changes as later wording builds on it, and its full image may appear only at the final word: al-Farazdaq’s هجائيا makes his threat specifically about the power of his satire.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r1.anchor: لا تتبين لك صورة المعنى الذي هو معنى الفرزدق إلا عند آخر حرف من البيت

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r2.claim: Al-Qaṭāmī’s line likewise reaches its intended image only with ذي الغلة, which identifies the thirsty person as the target of the water imagery.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r2.anchor: وجدتك لا تحصل على معنى يصح أن يقال إنه غرض الشاعر ومعناه إلا عند قوله : ' ذي الغلة ' .

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r3.claim: By contrast, in the three coordinated comparisons about fragrance, faces, and fingertips, each clause retains its meaning when the next is added.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r3.anchor: وذلك أنك ترى الذي تعقله من قوله : ' النشر مسك ' لا يصير بانضمام قوله : ' والوجوه دنانير ' إليه شيئا غير الذي كان

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r4.claim: Al-Jurjānī introduces Bashshār’s and Imruʾ al-Qays’s extended similes as further examples of poetry whose meaning depends on how its parts are composed.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p388/r4.anchor: فاعلم أن ما كان من الشعر مثل بيت بشار + الطويل + : ( كأن مثار النقع فوق رؤوسنا وأسيافنا ليل تهاوى كواكبه ) وقول امرىء القيس + الطويل + :

NASHR:v1p474/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p474/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p474/r1.claim: For open final hamza after alif, substitution is allowed with long or short length, and sometimes medium length; between-between also occurs, producing five possible forms in the cases discussed.
NASHR:v1p474/r1.anchor: ففيه البدل، ويجوز معه المد والقصر، وقد يجوز التوسط كما تقدم، فبقي ثلاثة أوجه

NASHR:v1p474/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p474/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p474/r2.claim: When the final hamza is kasra or damma, the same five forms apply if no written hamza sign is present; non-Hijazi readers add four forms, bringing the total to nine.
NASHR:v1p474/r2.anchor: فإن رسم للهمز فيه صورة جاز في المكسور منه نحو (وإيتاي ذي القربى، ومن آناي الليل)

NASHR:v1p474/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p474/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p474/r3.claim: The combinations multiply to eighteen for وايتاي and twenty-seven for ومن آناي when initial hamza treatment, pause, and transfer are counted; a damma case adds three rounded-waw options for a total of twelve.
NASHR:v1p474/r3.anchor: فيجيء معه المد والقصر، وفيه نظر فيصير خمسة، وتجيء هذه الخمسة بلا نظر

NASHR:v2p322/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p322/r2.speaker: الكسائي وأبو بكر
NASHR:v2p322/r2.claim: Al-Kisa'i and Abu Bakr read ترضى with ḍamma on tāʾ; the remaining readers use fatḥa.
NASHR:v2p322/r2.anchor: فقرأ الكسائي وأبو بكر بضم التاء، وقرأ الباقون

NASHR:v1p452/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p452/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p452/r1.claim: Four words with kasra hamza are written with a yāʾ image; the alif before them remains in the codices, though some copies omit it in the first two.
NASHR:v1p452/r1.anchor: والمكسورة صورت الهمزة فيه ياء في أربع كلمات بغير خلاف

NASHR:v1p452/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p452/r2.speaker: السخاوي
NASHR:v1p452/r2.claim: Al-Sakhāwī saw Syrian codices omit the alif in تلقاي and إيتاي, while retaining it in آناي الليل and وراي حجاب.
NASHR:v1p452/r2.anchor: قال السخاوي قد رأيت في المصحف الشامي الألف محذوفة

NASHR:v1p452/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p452/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p452/r5.claim: Among terminal hamzas preceded by fatḥa, ten words with ḍamma are written with wāw; examples include forms in Yūsuf, al-Naḥl, Ṭā Hā, al-Nūr, al-Furqān, and al-Muʾminūn.
NASHR:v1p452/r5.anchor: فالمضمومة عشرة كتبت الهمزة فيها واوا

NASHR:v1p460/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p460/r1.claim: When analogy favors a hamza easing that conflicts with the written form, the author prefers the easing that follows the codex, even if its analogy is weaker.
NASHR:v1p460/r1.anchor: إذا كان في التخفيف القياسي وجه راجح، وهو مخالف ظاهر الرسم، وكان الوجه الموافق ظاهره مرجوحا كان هذا الموافق الرسم هو المختار

NASHR:v1p460/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p460/r2.claim: Hamza easing may replace the consonant with pure wāw, yāʾ, or alif, or use between-between pronunciation, deletion, transfer, transfer with assimilation, or assimilation.
NASHR:v1p460/r2.anchor: فقد يكون ذلك بالواو المحضة نحو (يعبوا

NASHR:v1p460/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p460/r3.claim: The written yāʾ supports pure-yāʾ easing in من آناي الليل, a listed example of pronunciation matching the rasm.
NASHR:v1p460/r3.anchor: وقد يكون بالياء المحضة نحو (من نباي المرسلين

NASHR:v1p460/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p460/r4.claim: Other rasm-supported easing examples include between-between, deletion, transfer, transfer plus assimilation, and assimilation, each illustrated with Qurʾanic forms.
NASHR:v1p460/r4.anchor: وقد يكون بين بين نحو ما مثلنا به عند من وقف عليه بالروم الموافق للمصحف

NASHR:v1p460/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r5.speaker: أبو عبد الله بن شريح
NASHR:v1p460/r5.claim: Ibn Shurayḥ says Hamza should pause on a hamzated word using an easing that does not contradict the codex.
NASHR:v1p460/r5.anchor: قال أبو عبد الله بن شريح في كافيه: الاختيار عند القراء

NASHR:v1p460/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p460/r6.speaker: أبو عمرو الداني
NASHR:v1p460/r6.claim: Al-Dānī reports two approaches to final hamza written according to its vowel: the analogical approach changes it to an alif, while another approach substitutes the consonant shown by the rasm, such as wāw for الملؤا.
NASHR:v1p460/r6.anchor: فقال بعضهم: تسهيل الهمزة في جميع ذلك على حركة ما قبلها فتبدل ألفا ساكنة

NASHR:v1p200/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r1.claim: Ṭāʾ, dāl, and tāʾ exit from the tongue tip at the roots of the upper incisors; they are called natiʿiyya after the palate’s roof.
NASHR:v1p200/r1.anchor: من طرف اللسان وأصول الثنايا العليا

NASHR:v1p200/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r2.claim: Ṣād, sīn, and zāy exit just above the lower incisors and are called asaliyya; zāy may be named with a long vowel or as stressed zī.
NASHR:v1p200/r2.anchor: من بين طرف اللسان فويق الثنايا السفلى

NASHR:v1p200/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r3.claim: Ẓāʾ, dhāl, and thāʾ exit between the tongue tip and upper-incisor edges and are called lithawiyya, from the gum.
NASHR:v1p200/r3.anchor: من بين طرف اللسان وأطراف الثنايا العليا

NASHR:v1p200/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r4.claim: Fāʾ exits from the inner lower lip against the upper-incisor edges.
NASHR:v1p200/r4.anchor: من باطن الشفة السفلى وأطراف الثنايا العليا

NASHR:v1p200/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r5.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r5.claim: Non-lengthened wāw, bāʾ, and mīm exit between the lips; together with fāʾ they are the labial letters.

NASHR:v1p200/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r6.claim: Ghunna exits from the nasal cavity in nūn and mīm sākinah during concealment or assimilation with ghunna; the correct view is that their outlet shifts in those cases.
NASHR:v1p200/r6.anchor: وهو للغنة وهي تكون في النون والميم الساكنتين

NASHR:v1p200/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p200/r7.claim: The account excludes moving nūn; here the author means nūn sākinah pronounced clearly.
NASHR:v1p200/r7.anchor: خرج النون المتحركة، إنما يريد به النون الساكنة المظهرة

NASHR:v1p200/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r8.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v1p200/r8.claim: Sībawayh treats between-between hamza as one letter because he considers easing as a single general phenomenon; others count three letters by its alif, wāw, and yāʾ realizations.
NASHR:v1p200/r8.anchor: ومذهب سيبويه أنها حرف واحد نظرا إلى مطلق التسهيل، وذهب غيره إلى أنها ثلاثة أحرف

NASHR:v1p200/r9.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p200/r9.speaker: سيبويه
NASHR:v1p200/r9.claim: Imāla and tafkhīm are branches of the upright alif; Sībawayh counts only full imāla, treating strong imāla as another letter near yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p200/r9.anchor: ومنه ألفا الإمالة والتفخيم وهما فرعان عن الألف المنتصبة

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: الخليل
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: Khalīl explains the accusative in fronted exceptions such as ما فيها إلا أباك أحد by modeling a permissible order with the exception delayed: the excepted term normally follows negation as its badal, not as the term replaced.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: وزعم الخليل رحمه ~~الله أنهم إنما حملهم

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: كعب بن مالك
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: Sībawayh cites Kaʿb b. Mālik’s line, transmitted from trusted Arabs, as evidence for this exception usage and their aversion to reversing the normal badal relation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: قال كعب بن مالك PageV02P335 # % الناس ألب علينا فيك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: When a governor is already occupied and the exception follows, nominative or genitive case is allowed and the badal analysis is sound.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: كان الرفع والجر جائزين وحسن البدل لأنك

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: In من لي إلا أبوك صديقا, the preposition من is assigned to the father and is not left to govern it as a regular subject would be governed.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: وكذلك من لي إلا أبوك صديقا لأنك أخليت من للأب ولم تفرده لأن يعمل

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: بعضهم
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: Some grammarians prefer accusative when an exception is advanced, since they dislike putting a nominative predicate before the noun it describes.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: وقد قال بعضهم ما مررت بأحد إلا زيدا خير منه

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: يونس
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: Yūnus reports that trusted Arabs also say مالي إلا أبوك أحد, making أحد a badal; Sībawayh separately permits the accusative alternative صديقا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: يونس أن بعض العرب الموثوق بهم يقولون مالي إلا أبوك أحد

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: The accusative alternative مالي إلا أبوك صديقا is also possible, understood like لي أبوك صديقا.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: وإن شئت قلت مالي إلا أبوك صديقا

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.speaker: الكلحبة الثعلبي
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.claim: Sībawayh reads the poet’s line as an ellipsis, للمعصي أمر مضيعا, with مضيعا describing an understood أمر, like فيها رجل قائما.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابمايقدمفيهالمستثنى)#388/r.anchor: ومثله قول الشاعر وهو الكلحبة الثعلبي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r1.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r1.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r1.claim: Arabic has 29 basic letters and 35 when accepted subsidiary sounds are counted; these include forms used and approved in Qur’an recitation and poetry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r1.anchor: بحروف هن فروع وأصلها من التسعة والعشرين

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r2.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r2.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r2.claim: A total of 42 results when rare, disfavored sound variants are added; Sībawayh says these are not approved for Qur’an recitation or poetry.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r2.anchor: اثنين وأربعين حرفا بحروف غير مستحسنة ولا كثيرة في لغة من ترتضي

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r3.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r3.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r3.claim: The distinctions among these sounds are learned by direct oral transmission; weak ḍād may be articulated from either side of the tongue, with the left side easier for its described articulation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r3.anchor: الضاد الضعيفة تتكلف من الجانب الأيمن

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r4.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r4.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r4.claim: Sībawayh locates Arabic sounds at 16 articulation points, from three throat positions through tongue, teeth, lips, and the nasal passage, distinguishing the letters at each point.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r5.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r5.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r5.claim: He distinguishes 19 voiced letters from 10 whispered ones by airflow and articulatory pressure; nasalization in nūn and mīm can be demonstrated by holding the nose while speaking.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r5.anchor: حرف أشبع الاعتماد في موضعه ومنع النفس أن يجري

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r6.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r6.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r6.claim: He classifies sounds as stops, fricatives, intermediate ʿayn, lateral lām, nasal nūn and mīm, trilled rāʾ, and glide vowels; the descriptions identify what permits assimilation.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r6.anchor: وإنما وصفت لك حروف المعجم بهذه الصفات

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r7.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r7.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r7.claim: The emphatic letters are ṣād, ḍād, ṭāʾ, and ẓāʾ; without their emphatic articulation, ṭāʾ becomes dāl, ṣād sīn, ẓāʾ dhāl, and ḍād has no counterpart.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالإدغام)#806/r7.anchor: الصاد سينا والظاء ذالا ولخرجت الضاد من الكلام
